# Checkpoint 3 (1b): the top-level files the checks read, which a correction
# companion may supply when a verified copy was frozen in the wrong place.
CORRECTABLE = ("CODE_IDENTITY.txt", "RUN_LOG.txt", "CHANGE.diff", "APPROVAL_REPORT.md",
               "OUTGOING.txt", "SERVER_SUITE.txt", "ROSTER_COMPARISON.txt")


def corrections_map(root, corrections):
    """Checkpoint 3 (1b): misplaced verified evidence named by a correction
    companion. `corrections` is a directory outside the frozen packet holding
    ERRATA.md, whose lines `Relocated: NAME from PATH` say that the top-level
    file NAME was frozen at the packet-relative PATH instead, and a copy of
    it as corrections/NAME. The copy is used for NAME only when NAME is
    absent from the packet's top level, PATH is inside the packet and listed
    in its MANIFEST.sha256, PATH's own file name is NAME (checkpoint 5: a
    file frozen under another name, such as notes/draft.txt, cannot stand in
    for SERVER_SUITE.txt), no other line names the same PATH, and the copy's
    SHA-256 equals that listed hash (verify() has already matched the packet
    file to it). Anything else is refused, so no content enters that was not
    frozen and verified under that name. Other ERRATA.md lines are not read.
    Returns {NAME: copy path}."""
    if corrections is None:
        return {}
    if corrections.is_symlink() or not corrections.is_dir():
        fail("corrections must be an ordinary directory outside the packet")
    inside, packet = corrections.resolve(), root.resolve()
    if inside == packet or packet in inside.parents:
        fail("corrections directory must be outside the frozen packet")
    errata = corrections / "ERRATA.md"
    if errata.is_symlink() or not errata.is_file():
        fail("corrections directory needs an ordinary ERRATA.md")
    try:
        text = errata.read_bytes().decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        fail("ERRATA.md is not UTF-8")
    listed = dict(reversed(line.split("  ", 1)) for line in
                  (root / "MANIFEST.sha256").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines())
    found, sources = {}, set()
    for line in text.splitlines():
        match = re.fullmatch(r"Relocated: (\S+) from (\S+)\s*", line)
        if not match:
            continue
        name, source = match[1], match[2]
        if name not in CORRECTABLE:
            fail(f"ERRATA.md relocates a file the checker does not read: {name}")
        if name in found:
            fail(f"ERRATA.md relocates {name} twice")
        if (source.startswith("/") or "\\" in source
                or any(part in ("", ".", "..") for part in source.split("/"))):
            fail(f"ERRATA.md names a path outside the packet: {source}")
        if source not in listed:
            fail(f"ERRATA.md names a file not listed in the frozen manifest: {source}")
        if (root / name).exists() or (root / name).is_symlink():
            fail(f"ERRATA.md relocates {name}, but the packet has it at the top level")
        if source.split("/")[-1] != name:
            fail(f"ERRATA.md relocates {name} from a file of another name: {source}")
        if source in sources:
            fail(f"ERRATA.md names {source} for more than one file")
        sources.add(source)
        copy = corrections / name
        if copy.is_symlink() or not copy.is_file():
            fail(f"corrections directory has no ordinary copy of {name}")
        if digest(copy.read_bytes()) != listed[source]:
            fail(f"corrected copy of {name} differs from the frozen {source}")
        found[name] = copy
    return found


def code_identity(root, checked, changed, top=None):
    top = top or {}
    path = top.get("CODE_IDENTITY.txt", root / "CODE_IDENTITY.txt")
    log = top.get("RUN_LOG.txt", root / "RUN_LOG.txt")
    diff = top.get("CHANGE.diff", root / "CHANGE.diff")
    for required in (path, log, diff):
        if not required.is_file() or not required.stat().st_size:
            fail(f"missing or empty change evidence: {required.name}")
    report = top.get("APPROVAL_REPORT.md", root / "APPROVAL_REPORT.md")
    if not report.is_file() or report.is_symlink():
        fail("missing approval report")
    try:
        body = report.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        patch = diff.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        fail("approval report and change diff must be UTF-8")
    if ("## Exact tested changes" not in body or
            "## New tests" not in body or patch not in body):
        fail("approval report must contain the complete exact CHANGE.diff and new-test section")
    if not any(x.startswith("Full diff and exact new tests: ") and
               "APPROVAL_REPORT.md" in x for x in changed):
        fail("result must point to the complete approval report")
    try:
        entries = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        fail("code identity is not UTF-8")
    values = {}
    for line in entries:
        if ": " not in line:
            fail("malformed code identity")
        key, value = line.split(": ", 1)
        if key in values or not value.strip():
            fail("duplicate or empty code identity field")
        values[key] = value
    for key in ("base_commit", "tested_tree", "check", "outcome", "criterion_by",
                "test_written_by", "run_by"):
        if key not in values:
            fail(f"missing code identity field: {key}")
    if not re.fullmatch(HEX, values["base_commit"]) or not re.fullmatch(HEX, values["tested_tree"]):
        fail("invalid Git identity")
    outcome = values["outcome"]
    # A complete run count is as explicit as PASS; do not require a new
    # frozen packet merely to prefix an otherwise truthful outcome line.
    counts = [re.fullmatch(r"(?:(?:before|after|baseline|candidate) )?([1-9]\d*)/([1-9]\d*) exit 0",
                           part.strip(), re.I) for part in outcome.split(";")]
    counted_pass = all(match and match[1] == match[2] for match in counts)
    if not (re.match(r"^PASS(?:$|[ :])", outcome) or counted_pass):
        fail("result requires a passing recorded check")
    tested = [x for x in checked if x.startswith("Tested tree: ")]
    if tested != [f'Tested tree: {values["tested_tree"]}']:
        fail("screen tested tree does not match the evidence")


# Revision 17: a shell word for an absolute path, bare or quoted. Unquoted, only characters
# no supported shell treats specially (letters, digits and _ . / + @ % : , = -), which is
# tighter than revision 16's any non-space; anything else must be quoted. Inside single
# quotes nothing is special in sh, bash, zsh, csh or tcsh except the closing quote and csh's
# history character `!` (refused in every form); inside double quotes `$`, a backquote and a
# backslash are also refused. Revision 18 (repair 1, reading 1, finding 2; repair 1b): inside
# either kind of quotes every character must also be printable (str.isprintable: letters with
# accents and other scripts pass; tab, DEL and other control characters such as Ctrl-U, CR and ESC,
# format characters such as the bidi overrides U+202E and U+2066 and U+200B, line and paragraph
# separators, other non-space separators and surrogates do not), see printable_path(), so that a
# terminal or line editor has nothing to act on when the line is pasted; before, anything but the
# excluded characters and a newline.
SAFE_BARE = r"[A-Za-z0-9_./+@%:,=-]+"
QUOTED_SINGLE = r"[^'!]"  # with printable_path(): printable, except ' and !
QUOTED_DOUBLE = r"[^\"$`\\!]"  # also except " $ \ and a backquote
PATH_WORD = (r"(?:(?P<{0}_bare>/" + SAFE_BARE + r")|'(?P<{0}_single>/" + QUOTED_SINGLE + r"+)'"
             r"|\"(?P<{0}_double>/" + QUOTED_DOUBLE + r"+)\")")
# Revision 18: any absolute path to a Python 3 interpreter, by its file name: python, python3,
# python3.N or libtbx.python (a venv's bin/python, a system or Homebrew python3.N, the cctbx
# conda Python and the python that libtbx.python starts on macOS). Before: only
# /.../libtbx.python or /.../conda_base/bin/python3[.N].
INTERPRETER = re.compile(r"/.+/(?:python(?:3(?:\.\d+)?)?|libtbx\.python)")


def path_word(match, name):
    """The path a PATH_WORD group matched, without its quotes."""
    return next(match.group(f"{name}_{form}") for form in ("bare", "single", "double")
                if match.group(f"{name}_{form}") is not None)


def printable_path(path):
    """Revision 18 (repair 1b): every character printable (str.isprintable), as a quoted stop path
    needs; refuses control, format and separator characters other than the space, and surrogates."""
    return path.isprintable()


def stop_line(line):
    """The auto_start stop command: `INTERPRETER -I -B AUTO_QUEUE stop`, both absolute,
    each bare or quoted (a path with a space must be quoted); the interpreter is an
    existing executable regular file named python, python3, python3.N or libtbx.python
    (revision 18; before, only libtbx.python or conda_base/bin/python3[.N])."""
    match = re.fullmatch(PATH_WORD.format("python") + " -I -B " + PATH_WORD.format("queue")
                         + " stop", line)
    if not match or path_word(match, "queue") != str(AUTO_QUEUE):
        return False
    interpreter = path_word(match, "python")
    # Repair 1 (reading 1, finding 5): the checker accepts only what stop_command can write,
    # so a single quote (which stop_command cannot put inside single quotes) is refused in
    # the double-quoted form too.
    if "'" in interpreter or "'" in path_word(match, "queue"):
        return False
    if not (printable_path(interpreter) and printable_path(path_word(match, "queue"))):
        return False
    if not INTERPRETER.fullmatch(interpreter):
        return False
    resolved = os.path.realpath(interpreter)
    return os.path.isfile(resolved) and os.access(resolved, os.X_OK)


def stop_command(interpreter=None, queue=AUTO_QUEUE):
    """Revision 17: the stop line for the auto_start screen, each path bare when it has no
    space or quote, otherwise in single quotes; refused unless stop_line() accepts it (an
    absolute, existing, executable python, python3, python3.N or libtbx.python, revision 18).
    Revision 18: without an interpreter, the absolute sys.executable of the Python running
    this checker, which must then have psutil (the helper the stop line runs needs it)."""
    def word(path):
        path = str(path)
        return path if re.fullmatch(SAFE_BARE, path) else "'%s'" % path
    if interpreter is None:
        interpreter = sys.executable
        if not interpreter or not os.path.isabs(interpreter):
            fail("this Python reports no absolute interpreter path (sys.executable); "
                 "name the interpreter: stop-command INTERPRETER")
        if importlib.util.find_spec("psutil") is None:
            fail(f"this Python ({word(interpreter)}) has no psutil, which auto_queue.py needs: "
                 "make a venv and install it there (python3 -m venv DIR, then DIR/bin/python -m "
                 "pip install psutil; not --user, which the kit's -I ignores), then run this "
                 "command with DIR/bin/python")
    line = f"{word(interpreter)} -I -B {word(queue)} stop"
    if not stop_line(line):
        fail("the interpreter must be an absolute path to an existing executable Python 3 "
             "interpreter named python, python3, python3.N or libtbx.python, without a ' or ! "
             f"character or a character that is not printable: {interpreter!r}")
    return line


def auto_screen(kind, body, queue):
    """Auto screens: the start notice states its limits; the report repeats the helper's rows."""
    if kind == "auto_start":
        if queue:
            fail("auto_start has no queue to compare")
        # Revision 16: the stop command runs the helper with a Python that has psutil, by its
        # absolute path so that it works from any Terminal whatever PATH is (repair 1, finding
        # 3). Revision 18: any absolute python, python3, python3.N or libtbx.python (before,
        # only libtbx.python or conda_base/bin/python3[.N]); stop-command without an argument
        # prints the absolute sys.executable of the Python that runs it. A bare or relative
        # name is refused. Repair 2 (reading 2, finding 2): the interpreter must be an
        # existing, executable regular file (symbolic links resolved). Revision 17 (outside
        # reading of revision 16): either path may be written in single or double quotes,
        # which a path containing a space needs ('/Users/a b/.../libtbx.python' -I -B ...);
        # an unquoted path with a space, and a quoted relative or bare name, are refused.
        if not any(stop_line(line) for line in body["STOP"]):
            fail("auto_start needs the stop command of this procedure's auto_queue.py, run by an "
                 "existing executable interpreter")
        limits = " ".join(body["NOT AUTHORIZED"]).lower()
        if "master" not in limits or "publish" not in limits:
            fail("auto_start must say master is unchanged and nothing is published")
        text = " ".join(line for lines in body.values() for line in lines)
        if ("usage limit" not in text.lower() or not re.search(r"\bmanual(?:ly)?\b", text, re.IGNORECASE)
                or "/gc auto resume" not in text):
            fail("auto_start must say a usage limit stops the queue and resume is manual")
        return
    if queue is None:
        fail("auto_report requires --queue to compare with the queue record")
    helper = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", "-B", str(AUTO_QUEUE), "--queue", str(queue),
                             "report"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if helper.returncode == 18:
        # Revision 16: the helper needs psutil.
        fail("auto_queue.py report failed: " + (helper.stderr.strip().splitlines() or [""])[-1])
    if helper.returncode != 0:
        fail("auto_queue.py report failed")
    expected = [line for line in helper.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]
    if body["JOBS"] != expected:
        fail("JOBS does not repeat the queue report exactly")
    words = " ".join(body["IN SIMPLE WORDS"] + body["NEXT"])
    if re.search(r"\bstopped\b", words, re.IGNORECASE) and expected[0] != "**Stopped**":
        fail("says stopped but the queue report does not")
    if re.search(r"\bpassed\b", words, re.IGNORECASE) and not any("passed" in row for row in expected):
        fail("says passed but no job row does")
    approval_summaries(body["APPROVAL SUMMARIES"], ready_jobs(expected))


# Checkpoint 3: every verb form of integrate, merge, push and publish (the nouns
# "integration" and "publication" stay allowed, for PENDING and the follow-up note).
ACCEPT_CLAIMS = re.compile(r"\b(?:integrat(?:e|ed|es|ing)|merg(?:e|ed|es|ing)|"
                           r"push(?:ed|es|ing)?|publish(?:ed|es|ing)?)\b", re.IGNORECASE)


def accept_screen(body):
    """ACCEPT accepts one exact frozen candidate while the outside reading is
    pending. It names what is still pending, says that master and origin
    stay unchanged, and neither offers nor claims integration or
    publication (those are the RESULT and PUBLICATION decisions): any verb
    form of integrate, merge, push or publish is refused. Checkpoint 3: the
    DECISION's required words are now "master and origin stay unchanged"
    (replacing "merges nothing and publishes nothing", which used the
    refused verbs)."""
    text = "\n".join(line for lines in body.values() for line in lines)
    claim = ACCEPT_CLAIMS.search(text)
    if claim:
        fail(f"accept screen must not offer or claim integration or publication: {claim.group()!r}")
    if not any(re.fullmatch(r"Pending: \S.*", line) for line in body["PENDING"]):
        fail("accept screen needs a 'Pending:' line naming what is still pending")
    decision = " ".join(body["DECISION"]).lower()
    if "master and origin stay unchanged" not in decision:
        fail("accept DECISION must say master and origin stay unchanged")


SUMMARY_LABELS = ("Bug: ", "Fix: ", "Test: ", "Criterion: ", "Limits: ", "Approval: ")


def ready_jobs(rows):
    """Job ids of report rows whose step offers approval (or a provisional decision first)."""
    ready = []
    for row in rows:
        if row in ("| Job | Result | Decision or next step |", "| --- | --- | --- |"):
            continue
        cells = [c.strip() for c in row.strip().strip("|").split("|")]
        if len(cells) == 3 and (
                cells[2].startswith("approve for integration") or cells[2].startswith("decide P")):
            ready.append(cells[0].split()[0])
    return ready


def approval_summaries(section, ready):
    """One plain-words summary block per ready job, in report order; 'None ready.' otherwise."""
    if not ready:
        if section != ["None ready."]:
            fail("APPROVAL SUMMARIES must be 'None ready.' when no job is ready")
        return
    if len(section) != 7 * len(ready):
        fail("APPROVAL SUMMARIES needs exactly one seven-line block per ready job")
    for index, job in enumerate(ready):
        block = section[7 * index : 7 * index + 7]
        if not re.fullmatch(rf"Job {re.escape(job)}:.*", block[0]):
            fail(f"APPROVAL SUMMARIES block {index + 1} must start 'Job {job}:'")
        for label, line in zip(SUMMARY_LABELS, block[1:]):
            if not line.startswith(label) or not line[len(label):].strip():
                fail(f"summary for job {job} needs a non-empty '{label.strip()}' line in order")
        approval = block[6].lower()
        if "exact packet" not in approval or "merges nothing" not in approval:
            fail(f"summary for job {job}: Approval must say it accepts the exact packet and merges nothing")


def check(kind, screen, root=None, reading=None, disposition=None, report=True, queue=None,
          corrections=None, waiver=None):
    if not screen.is_file() or screen.is_symlink():
        fail("screen must be an ordinary file")
    try:
        # Bytes, so that a CR is seen rather than translated by universal newlines.
        source = screen.read_bytes().decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        fail("screen is not UTF-8")
    lines = source.splitlines()
    max_lines, max_words = BUDGET.get(kind, (28, 220))
    if len(lines) > max_lines or len(source.split()) > max_words:
        fail("screen exceeds one-page budget")
    if not lines or not source.endswith("\n") or "\r" in source:
        fail("screen needs LF lines and a final newline")
    if re.search(r"<[^>]+>|\{\{[^}]+\}\}", source):
        fail("unfilled placeholder")
    parts = lines[0].split(" | ")
    if kind in ("plan", "result"):
        expected = 3 if kind == "plan" else 4
        if len(parts) != expected or parts[0] != kind.upper() or not re.fullmatch(NAME, parts[1]) or parts[2] not in ("light", "full"):
            fail("invalid plan/result header")
    elif kind in ATTENTION:
        if len(parts) != 2 or parts[0] != kind.upper().replace("_", " ") or not re.fullmatch(NAME, parts[1]):
            fail("invalid auto header")
    elif kind in ("publication", "accept"):
        if len(parts) != 3 or parts[0] != kind.upper() or not re.fullmatch(NAME, parts[1]):
            fail(f"invalid {kind} header")
    elif len(parts) != 2 or parts[0] != "STOP" or not re.fullmatch(NAME, parts[1]):
        fail("invalid stop header")
    body = blocks(kind, lines)
    developer_view(kind, body)
    # Revision 17: the outside-reading waiver serves only a full-path RESULT, in place of a
    # reading; never with one, never with a disposition and never for publication.
    if waiver is not None:
        if reading is not None:
            fail("give either --reading or --waiver, not both")
        if disposition is not None:
            fail("a waiver replaces the reading; it takes no disposition")
        if kind == "result" and parts[2:3] == ["light"]:
            fail("--waiver serves only a full-path result; a light result defers its reading "
                 "to publication")
        if kind != "result" or parts[2:3] != ["full"]:
            fail("--waiver serves only a full-path result (integration); it never covers "
                 "publication")
    if kind in ATTENTION:
        if root or reading or disposition:
            fail("auto screens have no frozen evidence or outside reading")
        auto_screen(kind, body, queue)
    elif queue:
        fail("only auto_report compares with a queue")
    if kind in ("result", "publication", "accept"):
        if root is None or not re.fullmatch(SHA, parts[-1]):
            fail("evidence directory and manifest identity required")
        identity = verify(root)
        if parts[-1] != identity:
            fail("screen does not identify the current evidence")
        top = corrections_map(root, corrections)
        # Checkpoint 5 (review CP3 finding 5): post-reading errata are named in LIMITS.
        if top and not any("ERRATA.md" in line for line in body["LIMITS"]):
            fail("a correction companion was used: LIMITS must name ERRATA.md")
        if report:
            for name, copy in sorted(top.items()):
                print(f"NOTE {name} read from the correction companion {copy} "
                      "(byte-identical to the frozen file ERRATA.md names)")
        if kind == "accept":
            if reading or disposition:
                fail("accept is used while the outside reading is pending; it takes no reading")
            code_identity(root, body["CHECKED"], body["CANDIDATE"], top)
            accept_screen(body)
        elif kind == "result":
            code_identity(root, body["CHECKED"], body["CHANGED"], top)
            if parts[2] == "light":
                if reading or disposition or body["GATE"] != ["Reading: deferred to publication", "Verdict: deferred to publication"]:
                    fail("light-path outside reading belongs to publication batch")
            elif waiver is not None:
                waiver_matches(waiver, identity, body["GATE"], root)
                # The word WAIVED on a line naming the outside reading or review; "not WAIVED",
                # in any case, is refused (repair 1, reading 1 finding 10).
                if not any(re.search(r"\bWAIVED\b", line)
                           and not re.search(r"\bnot\s+WAIVED\b", line, re.I)
                           and re.search(r"\boutside (?:reading|review)\b", line, re.I)
                           for line in body["LIMITS"]):
                    fail("a waived outside reading must be named in LIMITS (WAIVED, on a line "
                         "naming the outside reading)")
            else:
                status = reading_matches("result", reading, identity, body["GATE"], disposition)
                if status in ("WAIVED", "PENDING") and not any(
                        status in line for heading in ("LIMITS", "DECISION")
                        for line in body[heading]):
                    fail("waived or pending condition must be visible in Developer View")
        else:
            # Checkpoint 3: companions inside the packet are refused here as in
            # check-draft (before, only the draft refused them).
            for name, _ in regular_files(root):
                if Path(name).name in COMPANION_NAMES:
                    fail(f"companion file inside the packet (keep it outside): {name}")
            for filename in ("SERVER_SUITE.txt", "ROSTER_COMPARISON.txt"):
                item = top.get(filename, root / filename)
                if not item.is_file() or not item.stat().st_size:
                    fail(f"missing or empty publication evidence: {filename}")
            batch = "\n".join(body["BATCH"])
            for block in parse_outgoing(top.get("OUTGOING.txt", root / "OUTGOING.txt")):
                if not re.search(rf"(?<![0-9A-Za-z]){block['commit']}(?![0-9A-Za-z])", batch):
                    fail("outgoing commit is not named in BATCH")
            suite_waiver(top.get("SERVER_SUITE.txt", root / "SERVER_SUITE.txt"))
            status = reading_matches("publication", reading, identity, body["GATE"], disposition)
            if status in ("WAIVED", "PENDING") and not any(
                    status in line for heading in ("LIMITS", "DECISION")
                    for line in body[heading]):
                fail("waived or pending condition must be visible in Developer View")
    elif kind not in ATTENTION and (root or reading or disposition):
        fail("plan and stop have no frozen evidence or outside reading")
    if corrections is not None and kind not in ("result", "publication", "accept"):
        fail("only result, publication and accept read a correction companion")
    if report:
        print(f"CHECK OK {kind}")
    return top if kind in ("result", "publication", "accept") else {}


PUBLICATION_FILES = ("OUTGOING.txt", "SERVER_SUITE.txt", "ROSTER_COMPARISON.txt")
PUBLICATION_LISTED = ("README_FIRST.md", "PROOF_SUMMARY.md", "APPROVAL_REPORT.md",
                      "PUBLICATION_NOTES.md")
COMPANION_NAMES = ("APPROVALS.md", "CHECKER.md", "ERRATA.md")


def check_draft(kind, root):
    """Run, on an unfrozen publication packet, every publication check that
    needs neither the freeze, the screen nor the outside reading (see
    payload/PUBLICATION_PACKET.md), and say which checks were skipped.

    Checkpoint 3: the OUTGOING.txt line rule (column-0 key lines of the
    seven keys, prose refused), the SERVER_SUITE.txt first-line form and
    the companion refusal are the final check's own rules (before, the draft
    alone applied the first and the last). A passing draft is not a frozen
    packet, a reading or a PUBLISH decision.
    """
    if kind != "publication":
        fail("check-draft supports only publication")
    files = dict(regular_files(root))
    for name in PUBLICATION_FILES:
        item = root / name
        if name not in files or not item.stat().st_size:
            fail(f"missing or empty publication evidence at the packet top level: {name}")
    for name in files:
        if Path(name).name in COMPANION_NAMES:
            fail(f"companion file inside the packet (keep it outside): {name}")
    blocks = parse_outgoing(root / "OUTGOING.txt")
    suite_waiver(root / "SERVER_SUITE.txt")
    print(f"DRAFT OK publication ({len(blocks)} outgoing repository block(s))")
    print("checked: OUTGOING.txt key lines and blocks, SERVER_SUITE.txt and "
          "ROSTER_COMPARISON.txt at top level, SERVER_SUITE first line and NOT RUN waiver "
          "form, no companions inside")
    if "MANIFEST.sha256" in files:
        verify(root)
        print("checked: existing MANIFEST.sha256 matches the files")
    else:
        print("skipped: freeze and packet identity (not frozen)")
    print("skipped: outgoing commits named in BATCH (needs the PUBLICATION screen)")
    print("skipped: outside reading, its scope and any disposition (needs the reading)")
    for name in PUBLICATION_LISTED:
        if name not in files:
            print(f"NOTE not present (listed in PUBLICATION_PACKET.md, not checked): {name}")


def present(kind, screen, root=None, reading=None, disposition=None, queue=None,
            corrections=None, waiver=None):
    """Check the saved decision, then render a conspicuous Developer view."""
    top = check(kind, screen, root, reading, disposition, report=False, queue=queue,
                corrections=corrections, waiver=waiver)
    lines = screen.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    if kind == "plan" or kind in ATTENTION:
        spaced = []
        for line in lines:
            if line in HEADINGS[kind]:
                spaced.append("")
            spaced.append(line)
        lines = spaced
    if kind in ("result", "publication", "accept"):
        lines[0] = " | ".join(lines[0].split(" | ")[:-1])
    lines = [line for line in lines if not line.startswith(
        ("Tested tree: ", "Reading SHA256: ", "Disposition SHA256: ", "Waiver SHA256: "))]
    lines = [DISPLAY_ID.sub(
        lambda match: "[recorded]" if any(c in "abcdef" for c in match.group())
        else match.group(), line) for line in lines]
    body = "\n".join(lines)
    # A longer outer fence keeps any backticks in a screen inside its body.
    longest = max((len(match.group()) for match in re.finditer(r"`+", body)), default=0)
    fence = "`" * max(3, longest + 1)
    print(ATTENTION.get(kind, "**PLEASE READ — YOUR DECISION IS NEEDED**") + "\n\n" +
          fence + "\n" + body + "\n" + fence)
    # Checkpoint 5 (review CP3 finding 5): the rendered screen says that a
    # correction companion supplied evidence, and names it.
    for name, copy in sorted(top.items()):
        print(f"NOTE: correction companion used: {name} was read from {copy} "
              f"(ERRATA.md in {copy.parent}; byte-identical to the frozen file it names)")


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    for name in ("freeze", "verify"):
        commands.add_parser(name).add_argument("evidence", type=Path)
    commands.add_parser("verify-source").add_argument("source", type=Path)
    commands.add_parser("check-claude-version")
    commands.add_parser("register-skill").add_argument("source", type=Path)
    commands.add_parser("stop-command", help="revision 17: print the auto_start stop line, "
                        "quoting a path that needs it; revision 18: without INTERPRETER, the "
                        "absolute path of the Python running this command").add_argument(
                            "interpreter", nargs="?")
    draft = commands.add_parser("check-draft")
    draft.add_argument("kind", choices=("publication",))
    draft.add_argument("evidence", type=Path)
    command = commands.add_parser("check")
    presenter = commands.add_parser("present")
    for command in (command, presenter):
        command.add_argument("kind", choices=tuple(HEADINGS))
        command.add_argument("screen", type=Path)
        command.add_argument("--evidence", type=Path)
        command.add_argument("--reading", type=Path)
        command.add_argument("--disposition", type=Path)
        command.add_argument("--queue", type=Path)
        command.add_argument("--corrections", type=Path,
                             help="correction companion directory (ERRATA.md and byte-identical "
                                  "copies of misplaced frozen files), outside the packet")
        command.add_argument("--waiver", type=Path,
                             help="revision 17: OUTSIDE_WAIVER.md, the Developer's waiver of the "
                                  "outside reading for a full-path result; not with --reading")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    try:
        if args.command == "freeze":
            freeze(args.evidence)
        elif args.command == "verify":
            verify(args.evidence)
            print("VERIFIED evidence")
        elif args.command == "verify-source":
            verify_source(args.source)
            print("VERIFIED complete source")
        elif args.command == "check-claude-version":
            check_claude_version()
        elif args.command == "register-skill":
            register_skill(args.source)
        elif args.command == "stop-command":
            print(stop_command(args.interpreter))
        elif args.command == "check-draft":
            check_draft(args.kind, args.evidence)
        elif args.command == "check":
            check(args.kind, args.screen, args.evidence, args.reading, args.disposition,
                  queue=args.queue, corrections=args.corrections, waiver=args.waiver)
        else:
            present(args.kind, args.screen, args.evidence, args.reading, args.disposition,
                    queue=args.queue, corrections=args.corrections, waiver=args.waiver)
    except (ValueError, OSError) as error:
        print(f"ERROR: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

tests/auto_queue_standin.py

"""Test-only launcher for auto_queue.py (Revision 12). Not part of the helper.

The kit tests use it, instead of running auto_queue.py itself, only where the
platform is not macOS (real, or simulated inside the test processes with
GC_TEST_SIMULATE_NON_MACOS=1, a variable read only by the tests). It imports
auto_queue and, inside this one process only, (a) accepts the platform and
(b) replaces /usr/bin/sandbox-exec with a stand-in that checks the
`-p PROFILE CMD...` form, ignores the profile and executes CMD unrestricted
(in the same process, as sandbox-exec does). The installed auto_queue.py has
no hook, variable or option for this; run directly, auto_queue.py refuses
`run` off macOS.

This launcher refuses real queues (Revision 12, P8). Before it imports the
helper, starts anything or writes anything, it exits 16 unless every queue
path it checks (the helper home, every --queue, the queue named by the home's
ACTIVE file, and init's records root and lock directory) lies inside one
directory directly under the temporary
directory (tempfile.gettempdir()) that holds the test-only marker file
GC_KIT_TEST_QUEUE_ROOT with exactly MARKER_TEXT. It resolves those paths as
auto_queue.py does: the helper home is --home, else GC_AUTO_HOME, else the
default home, which is refused. An empty or blank --home, --queue, --records
or --lock-dir, or an empty or blank GC_AUTO_HOME used as the home, is refused
too, so that the paths checked are the ones the helper opens: the helper
treats a blank value (for example --home " ") as a relative path, falls back
to another home for an empty --home or GC_AUTO_HOME (and to the ACTIVE queue
for an empty --queue), resolves an empty --records to the current directory,
and refuses an empty --lock-dir itself. Checked: every --home or GC_AUTO_HOME, every
--queue, the queue named by each home's ACTIVE file, and init's --records and
--lock-dir. The kit tests write the marker into the temporary directory they
create for each test; real queues (under .claude/records, ~/GuidedCoding/auto
or anywhere else without it) are refused. Limits: a marker written by hand
inside the temporary directory is accepted, and so is a symlink planted by
hand inside a marked test queue (for example its runs/ pointing to a real
queue's runs/, which then receives the run record), because the check
resolves the queue directory, not what is inside it. This guards against
mistaken use, not deliberate misuse. Only those queue paths are checked:
other paths the helper opens or writes (--log, --cwd, --file, --packet,
--script, --grant, --jobs) are not, so a run started through the launcher
can write its log anywhere.

Because the stand-in does not block the network, the tests run through it
only controlled local commands; the tests of the real network block and of
the `ps -E` run-id marker are skipped off macOS.

    libtbx.python -I -B auto_queue_standin.py [auto_queue.py arguments]
"""

import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import types

STANDIN = os.path.realpath(__file__)
FLAG = "--sandbox-standin"
MARKER = "GC_KIT_TEST_QUEUE_ROOT"
MARKER_TEXT = "guided_coding kit tests: test-only queue root for this test run; never a real queue\n"
REFUSED = 16


def sandbox_standin(argv):
    """Stand-in for `sandbox-exec -p PROFILE CMD [ARG...]`."""
    if len(argv) < 3 or argv[0] != "-p":
        print("sandbox stand-in: expected -p PROFILE CMD [ARG...]", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    try:
        os.execvp(argv[2], argv[2:])
    except OSError as error:
        print("sandbox stand-in: cannot run %s: %s" % (argv[2], error), file=sys.stderr)
        return 127


def option_values(argv, name):
    """Every value given as `NAME VALUE` or `NAME=VALUE` before `--` (the helper's
    parsers use allow_abbrev=False, so no other spelling reaches it)."""
    tokens = argv[:argv.index("--")] if "--" in argv else argv
    values = []
    for index, token in enumerate(tokens):
        if token == name and index + 1 < len(tokens):
            values.append(tokens[index + 1])
        elif token.startswith(name + "="):
            values.append(token[len(name) + 1:])
    return values


def test_root(path, temp):
    """The directory directly under `temp` that contains `path` (resolved), or None."""
    real = os.path.realpath(path)
    if os.path.commonpath([real, temp]) != temp or real == temp:
        return None
    return os.path.join(temp, os.path.relpath(real, temp).split(os.sep)[0])


def marked(root):
    marker = os.path.join(root, MARKER)
    if os.path.islink(marker) or not os.path.isfile(marker):
        return False
    try:
        with open(marker, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            return handle.read() == MARKER_TEXT
    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
        return False


def not_a_test_queue(argv, environ):
    """None when every checked queue path (helper home, --queue, the ACTIVE queue,
    init's --records and --lock-dir) is inside one marked test root; else the
    reason. Other paths (--log, --cwd, --file, ...) are not checked. Mirrors auto_queue.home_dir/open_queue. An empty or blank
    value is refused here: the helper would read it as absent, as the current
    directory or as a relative path, not as the value checked here."""
    temp = os.path.realpath(tempfile.gettempdir())
    for name in ("--home", "--queue", "--records", "--lock-dir"):
        if any(not value.strip() for value in option_values(argv, name)):
            return ("empty or blank %s (refused so that the paths checked are the ones "
                    "the helper opens)" % name)
    homes = option_values(argv, "--home")
    if not homes:
        if not environ.get("GC_AUTO_HOME", "").strip():
            return ("no helper home given (a non-empty --home or GC_AUTO_HOME); "
                    "the default home is refused")
        homes = [environ["GC_AUTO_HOME"]]
    paths = [("helper home", home) for home in homes]
    paths += [("queue", queue) for queue in option_values(argv, "--queue")]
    for home in homes:
        active = os.path.join(home, "ACTIVE")
        if os.path.isfile(active):
            with open(active, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as handle:
                lines = handle.read().splitlines()
            if lines and lines[0].strip():
                paths.append(("queue named by ACTIVE", lines[0].strip()))
    paths += [("records root", value) for value in option_values(argv, "--records")]
    paths += [("lock directory", value) for value in option_values(argv, "--lock-dir")]
    roots = set()
    for what, path in paths:
        root = test_root(path, temp)
        if root is None:
            return "%s %s is not inside the temporary directory %s" % (what, path, temp)
        if not marked(root):
            return "%s %s: %s has no test-only marker %s" % (what, path, root, MARKER)
        roots.add(root)
    if len(roots) != 1:
        return "the queue paths are in different test directories: %s" % ", ".join(sorted(roots))
    return None


def launch(argv):
    reason = not_a_test_queue(argv, os.environ)
    if reason:
        print("REFUSED: tests/auto_queue_standin.py is a test-only launcher and runs only "
              "queues the kit's own tests created; nothing was started or recorded. Use "
              "auto_queue.py for real queues. Not a test queue: %s" % reason, file=sys.stderr)
        return REFUSED
    sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(STANDIN)))
    import auto_queue
    auto_queue.platform_supported = lambda: True
    auto_queue.SANDBOX = STANDIN

    def popen(args, *more, **options):
        if isinstance(args, (list, tuple)) and args and args[0] == STANDIN:
            args = [sys.executable, "-I", "-B", STANDIN, FLAG] + list(args[1:])
        return subprocess.Popen(args, *more, **options)

    names = {name: getattr(subprocess, name) for name in dir(subprocess)
             if not name.startswith("__")}
    names["Popen"] = popen
    auto_queue.subprocess = types.SimpleNamespace(**names)
    return auto_queue.main(argv)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if sys.argv[1:2] == [FLAG]:
        sys.exit(sandbox_standin(sys.argv[2:]))
    sys.exit(launch(sys.argv[1:]))

tests/tst_auto_queue_v20.py

"""Controls for the claims that auto_queue.py makes (stage1/AUTO_QUEUE_SPEC.md,
including its Revision 2 section, which overrides the earlier text).

Claims controlled: ACTIVE resolution, init refusals, legal and illegal
transitions, atomic-write leftovers, run records and exit status, the run
refusal order (stop, lock, floor, criterion/candidate, allowed roots) and the
Revision 2 run preconditions (job state, this job's worker), stale runs after a
criterion or candidate change, the Ready-for-approval and Approved conditions
(worker or live run, whole-token quote, re-check), interrupted and
group-left-running runs, stop / check-stop / reconcile with real processes
(also from a different TZ, locale and PATH, and during the probe), the worker
registry, the queue lock (queue_dir ownership, extra files), and a truthful report.
Revision 9: the packet's SCREENING.txt (form, line numbers, included test, outside
access against the network grant, re-check at Approved and in the report) and the
manual-resume Waiting step.

The tool is only ever run through subprocess (-I -B); the test process never
imports it or reads its source. Every queue, control home, lock directory, space path,
allowed root and git repository lives under a temporary directory; --home and
--lock-dir are always passed, so the default home is never touched.
Each refusal is paired with a positive control (the same call without the
forbidden condition is accepted).
Revision 12: `run` needs macOS. Off macOS (real, or simulated inside the test
processes with GC_TEST_SIMULATE_NON_MACOS=1) the helper is run through the
test-only launcher tests/auto_queue_standin.py, whose stand-in for sandbox-exec
runs commands unrestricted; every command run through it is local. Only the
tests of the real macOS mechanisms (and their duplicates) are skipped there, each
with its reason (GUIDED_CODING_VERIFICATION.md lists them). The refusal tests
run the real helper (a subprocess that imports it and sets sys.platform), never
the launcher. `init` without --lock-dir is refused. The launcher cannot run a
real queue job (P8): it refuses (exit 16) any queue outside a temporary
directory of this test run that holds the test-only marker, which setUp writes.
P9: one test reads the helper's own process table (auto_queue.snapshot(), in a
subprocess that imports the helper) and checks that it lists a test process with
its parent and group, and that cleanup ends that process.
P10: the helper allows one second on the earlier bound of a run's window, because
Linux ps can report a start time up to 1 s early. On the Mac the tests imitate that
inside a test-side launcher (LINUX_PS_SCRIPT: the helper's ps start times are taken
as floor(exact fork time - 0.8 s) and its `ps -E` markers are dropped, as on Linux);
four tests use it always, and GC_TEST_IMITATE_LINUX_PS=1 (read only by the tests) runs
every helper call of a selected test through it. Off the Mac the launcher changes
nothing: real Linux ps already reports early.
Revision 16: the helper reads the process table through psutil, not /bin/ps; so do the
tests' own process checks (psutil in this test process; /proc on Linux where it was used
before). Unreadable-table controls make psutil fail inside the helper's own process
(FAULT_SETUP: psutil.pids, or one Process field, raising AccessDenied, ZombieProcess or
NoSuchProcess, or os.getpgid failing), never the installed helper. Without psutil in this
interpreter the module runs only the PsutilMissing tests (the helper stops with exit 18; the
rest is skipped with the reason). Tests that need git (the queue repository, candidates)
skip with GIT_SKIP when git is not on PATH; tests that run sandbox-exec skip without
/usr/bin/sandbox-exec. The suite now also runs inside sandbox-exec, where /bin/ps is refused
but psutil reads the table.
"""

import calendar
import errno
import fcntl
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
import shlex
import shutil
import socket
import struct
import re
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

try:
    import psutil  # Revision 16: the helper requires it, and the tests' own checks use it
except ImportError:
    psutil = None

TOOL = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "auto_queue.py"
# Revision 12: the test-only launcher, used only where the platform is not macOS
# (real, or simulated with GC_TEST_SIMULATE_NON_MACOS=1, read only by the tests).
STANDIN = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "auto_queue_standin.py"
NON_MACOS = sys.platform != "darwin" or os.environ.get("GC_TEST_SIMULATE_NON_MACOS") == "1"
# Revision 12 (P8): the launcher runs only queues inside a directory directly under the
# temporary directory that holds this marker (written by setUp); otherwise exit 16.
STANDIN_MARKER = "GC_KIT_TEST_QUEUE_ROOT"
STANDIN_MARKER_TEXT = "guided_coding kit tests: test-only queue root for this test run; never a real queue\n"
STANDIN_REFUSED = 16
STANDIN_MESSAGE = ("REFUSED: tests/auto_queue_standin.py is a test-only launcher and runs only "
                   "queues the kit's own tests created; nothing was started or recorded.")
MACOS_ONLY = "macOS mechanism, skipped off macOS: "
# Revision 16: git and sandbox-exec are optional for the suite. A test that needs one skips
# with these reasons when it is missing (git: not on PATH; sandbox-exec: the helper runs
# /usr/bin/sandbox-exec by that path, so PATH does not hide it; GC_TEST_NO_SANDBOX_EXEC=1,
# read only by the tests, makes the tests treat it as missing, as a control of the skips).
GIT = shutil.which("git")
GIT_SKIP = ("git not on PATH: this test needs a git repository (queue candidates, packet "
            "trees); the helper refuses `candidate` without git (exit 2)")
SANDBOX_EXEC = "/usr/bin/sandbox-exec"
NO_SANDBOX_EXEC = (not os.path.exists(SANDBOX_EXEC)
                   or os.environ.get("GC_TEST_NO_SANDBOX_EXEC") == "1")
SANDBOX_SKIP = ("/usr/bin/sandbox-exec missing: this test runs the real sandbox-exec (the "
                "helper refuses a blocked-network run without it, exit 14)")
_SANDBOX_STATE = []


def sandbox_exec_problem():
    """Revision 16: None when /usr/bin/sandbox-exec can apply a profile here; else why not:
    missing (SANDBOX_SKIP), or refused as inside another sandbox-exec, which cannot apply a
    second profile ("sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted", exit 71). Checked once."""
    if not _SANDBOX_STATE:
        problem = SANDBOX_SKIP if NO_SANDBOX_EXEC else None
        if problem is None:
            try:
                probe = subprocess.run([SANDBOX_EXEC, "-p", "(version 1)(allow default)",
                                        sys.executable, "-c", "pass"], capture_output=True,
                                       text=True, timeout=60)
            except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as error:
                problem = "sandbox-exec could not be run: %s" % error
            else:
                if probe.returncode != 0:
                    problem = ("sandbox-exec cannot apply a profile here (exit %d: %s), as inside "
                               "another sandbox-exec; this test needs the real network block"
                               % (probe.returncode, probe.stderr.strip()[:120] or "no message"))
        _SANDBOX_STATE.append(problem)
    return _SANDBOX_STATE[0]
# Revision 18: the message names this Python's own install command (the helper runs with the
# tests' sys.executable) and libtbx.python, and no longer names cctbx; repair 1: the venv route.
# Repair 1 (reading 1, finding 1): the venv route (pip may refuse an externally managed Python,
# and a --user install is invisible under -I).
VENV_ROUTE = ("make a venv and install it there (python3 -m venv DIR, then DIR/bin/python -m pip "
              "install psutil; not --user, which the kit's -I ignores), then run with DIR/bin/python; "
              "or use libtbx.python")
PSUTIL_MISSING, PSUTIL_MESSAGE = 18, (
    "REFUSED: requires psutil, which %s does not have: %s"
    % (sys.executable if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_./+@%:,=-]+", sys.executable)
       else "'%s'" % sys.executable, VENV_ROUTE))
PLATFORM_REFUSED = 15
PLATFORM_MESSAGE = "REFUSED: auto-mode runs need macOS (sandbox-exec and `ps -E`); this system is "
# The real helper with non-macOS forced inside its own process (no option or variable).
FORCED_NON_MACOS = ("import sys; sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1]); import auto_queue; "
                    "sys.platform = 'linux'; sys.exit(auto_queue.main(sys.argv[2:]))")
QID = "q1"
ALPHA, BETA = "job-alpha", "job-beta"
JOBS = [{"id": ALPHA, "title": "Alpha", "requires": ["unit", "build"], "depends_on": []},
        {"id": BETA, "title": "Beta", "requires": ["unit"], "depends_on": []}]
REPORT_HEADER = "| Job | Result | Decision or next step |"
WAITING_STEP = ("resume with /gc auto resume after the reset "
                "(automatic continuation is not supported)")
TIMEOUT = 15
# A CMD (or grandchild) that signals readiness and exits 0 once the release file
# appears (safety deadline 30 s; 120 s with the flag `long`, revision 14). mode is
# `+`-joined flags: `ignore`: SIGTERM ignored; `exit0`: SIGTERM exits 0 (a test
# script that traps TERM); `note`: SIGTERM writes <ready>.term and is otherwise
# ignored; `pgrp`: move to a new process group (same session); `setsid`: new
# session; `default`: SIGTERM kills it.
WAIT_SCRIPT = """import os, signal, sys, time
mode, ready, release = sys.argv[1:4]
flags = set(mode.split("+"))
if "ignore" in flags:
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIG_IGN)
elif "exit0" in flags:
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, lambda *_: sys.exit(0))
elif "note" in flags:
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, lambda *_: open(ready + ".term", "w").close())
if "pgrp" in flags:
    os.setpgid(0, 0)
if "setsid" in flags:
    os.setsid()
open(ready, "w").close()
deadline = time.time() + (120 if "long" in flags else 30)
while not os.path.exists(release) and time.time() < deadline:
    time.sleep(0.05)
"""
# A CMD that starts children (inheriting its group), writes their pids, then
# exits 0 (`exit`) or stays until the deadline (`hold`).
LAUNCH_SCRIPT = """import os, subprocess, sys, time
end, wait, pids = sys.argv[1:4]

children = [subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, wait, *spec], stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                             stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
            for spec in specs]
deadline = time.time() + 10
while not all(os.path.exists(s[1]) for s in specs) and time.time() < deadline:
    time.sleep(0.05)
with open(pids + ".tmp", "w") as handle:
    handle.write(" ".join(str(child.pid) for child in children))
os.replace(pids + ".tmp", pids)
if end == "hold":
    time.sleep(30)

# Revision 16 (replaces the Revision 13 ps stand-ins, which tested a ps the helper no longer
# runs): psutil failures made inside the helper's own process only. FAULT_SETUP defines
# install_faults(spec): spec["pids"] makes psutil.pids() return [] ("empty") or raise
# AccessDenied, ZombieProcess, NoSuchProcess or OSError; spec["fields"] maps a psutil.Process
# method (status, ppid, create_time, num_threads, environ, cmdline) or "pgid" (os.getpgid) to
# the error it raises for the processes chosen by spec["who"] ("all", "own", "others", one
# pid or a list of pids; repair 1: also RuntimeError, and "DropMarker" for environ, which then
# returns the environment without GC_AUTO_RUN_ID); spec["exists"] fixes psutil.pid_exists() for them (the re-check after
# NoSuchProcess); with spec["once"] each field fails only on its first read of each process;
# spec["platform"] sets sys.platform in that process (probes only). Repair 2: a create_time
# fault also hits the helper's kernel_start (its macOS start time) when it is imported.
FAULT_SETUP = """import os, sys
import psutil
def install_faults(spec):
    me = os.getpid()
    fired = set()
    def fire(field, pid):
        if not spec.get("once"):
            return True
        if (field, pid) in fired:
            return False
        fired.add((field, pid))
        return True
    def hit(pid):
        who = spec.get("who", "all")
        return bool(pid) and (who == "all" or (who == "own" and pid == me)
                              or (who == "others" and pid != me) or who == pid
                              or (isinstance(who, list) and pid in who))
    def error(name, pid):
        if name == "OSError":
            return PermissionError(1, "Operation not permitted (test fault)")
        if name == "RuntimeError":
            return RuntimeError("synthetic test fault")
        return getattr(psutil, name)(pid)
    pids = spec.get("pids")
    if pids == "empty":
        psutil.pids = lambda: []
    elif pids:
        def failing_pids():
            raise error(pids, 0)
        psutil.pids = failing_pids
    for field, name in spec.get("fields", {}).items():
        if field == "pgid":
            real_getpgid = os.getpgid
            def getpgid(pid, real=real_getpgid, name=name):
                if hit(pid) and fire("pgid", pid):
                    if name == "NoSuchProcess":
                        raise ProcessLookupError(3, "No such process (test fault)")
                    if name == "RuntimeError":
                        raise RuntimeError("synthetic test fault")
                    raise PermissionError(1, "Operation not permitted (test fault)")
                return real(pid)
            os.getpgid = getpgid
            continue
        helper = sys.modules.get("auto_queue")
        if field == "create_time" and helper is not None and hasattr(helper, "kernel_start"):
            # Repair 2: on macOS the helper reads the start time from the kernel record.
            real_start = helper.kernel_start
            def kernel_start(pid, real=real_start, name=name):
                if hit(pid) and fire("create_time", pid):
                    raise error(name, pid)
                return real(pid)
            helper.kernel_start = kernel_start
        real = getattr(psutil.Process, field)
        def method(self, *args, real=real, name=name, field=field, **kwargs):
            if hit(self.pid) and fire(field, self.pid):
                if name == "DropMarker":  # environ without the run-id marker
                    return {k: v for k, v in real(self, *args, **kwargs).items()
                            if k != "GC_AUTO_RUN_ID"}
                raise error(name, self.pid)
            return real(self, *args, **kwargs)
        for attribute in ("cache_activate", "cache_deactivate"):  # psutil's oneshot() cache
            if hasattr(real, attribute):
                setattr(method, attribute, getattr(real, attribute))
        setattr(psutil.Process, field, method)
    if "exists" in spec:
        real_exists = psutil.pid_exists
        def exists(pid):
            if hit(pid):
                if spec["exists"] == "RuntimeError":
                    raise RuntimeError("synthetic test fault")
                return spec["exists"]
            return real_exists(pid)
        psutil.pid_exists = exists
    if spec.get("platform"):
        sys.platform = spec["platform"]
"""

MT_SCRIPT = """import ctypes, os, signal, sys, threading, time

        n += 1

            handle.write(str(n))
        os.replace(beat + ".tmp", beat)
        time.sleep(0.1)
    os._exit(0)

time.sleep(0.3)
ctypes.CDLL(None, use_errno=True).syscall(SYS_EXIT, 0)

# Revision 15 (review finding 1): a platform /bin/sh (and /bin/sleep) shows no environment to
# `ps -E` on macOS, so the helper cannot see a run-id marker on it and must find it through the
# wrapper's tracked descendants. The stand-in therefore first re-executes itself (same pid,
# start time and parent) with the marker moved to another variable, so that its own visible
# environment has no marker; each command runs as its child with the marker restored, except a
# command flagged "platform" (standing in for a platform binary such as /bin/sleep), which runs
# without it. Review finding 3: with "exec_last" the last command replaces the stand-in
# (os.execve), as bash 5.1 and later and dash do with the last simple command of `sh -c 'a; b'`;
# otherwise it runs as a child and the stand-in waits, as macOS /bin/sh (bash 3.2) and the bash
# 4.2 of cci-gpu-00 do. The exit status is the last command's.
SHELL_STANDIN = """import json, os, subprocess, sys
MARKER, KEPT = "GC_AUTO_RUN_ID", "GC_TEST_STANDIN_KEPT_RUN_ID"
if MARKER in os.environ:
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env[KEPT] = env.pop(MARKER)
    os.execve(sys.executable, [sys.executable] + sys.argv, env)
spec = json.loads(sys.argv[1])


def environment(platform):
    env = {key: value for key, value in os.environ.items() if key != KEPT}
    if KEPT in os.environ and not platform:
        env[MARKER] = os.environ[KEPT]
    return env


code, commands = 0, spec["commands"]
for index, command in enumerate(commands):
    env = environment(command.get("platform", False))
    if spec.get("exec_last") and index == len(commands) - 1:
        os.execve(command["argv"][0], command["argv"], env)
    code = subprocess.call(command["argv"], env=env)
sys.exit(code)
"""

# stand-in launcher, which then imports this already patched module) with Linux procps start
# times imitated inside this one process: every ps start time the helper reads (snapshot() and
# process_start()) becomes floor(exact fork time - LAG), the way procps adds clock ticks to a
# boot time truncated to whole seconds, and the `ps -E` markers are dropped (Linux ps has no
# -E). The exact fork time comes from the macOS kernel (sysctl KERN_PROC_PID, p_starttime).
# Off macOS it changes nothing. The installed helper is never changed.
IMITATE_LINUX_PS = os.environ.get("GC_TEST_IMITATE_LINUX_PS") == "1"
LINUX_PS_LAG = 0.8
LINUX_PS_SCRIPT = """import ctypes, math, os, runpy, sys, time
kit, helper, lag = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], float(sys.argv[3])
sys.path.insert(0, kit)
import auto_queue
if sys.platform == "darwin":
    libc = ctypes.CDLL(None)
    real_snapshot, real_process_start = auto_queue.snapshot, auto_queue.process_start

    def lagged(pid):
        mib = (ctypes.c_int * 4)(1, 14, 1, int(pid))  # CTL_KERN, KERN_PROC, KERN_PROC_PID
        buf, size = ctypes.create_string_buffer(1024), ctypes.c_size_t(1024)
        if libc.sysctl(mib, 4, buf, ctypes.byref(size), None, 0) != 0 or size.value < 16:
            return None
        sec = int.from_bytes(buf.raw[0:8], "little", signed=True)
        usec = int.from_bytes(buf.raw[8:12], "little", signed=True)
        return int(math.floor(sec + usec / 1e6 - lag)) if sec > 0 else None

    def snapshot():
        # Revision 14: any further fields (the zombie flag) are kept as they are.
        return {pid: [ppid, pgid, sid, None if start is None else lagged(pid), set(), *rest]
                for pid, (ppid, pgid, sid, start, marks, *rest) in real_snapshot().items()}

    def process_start(pid):
        text = real_process_start(pid)
        if text in (None, auto_queue.UNREADABLE):
            return text
        start = lagged(pid)
        return text if start is None else time.strftime("%a %b %d %H:%M:%S %Y", time.gmtime(start))

    auto_queue.snapshot, auto_queue.process_start = snapshot, process_start
sys.argv = [helper] + sys.argv[4:]
if os.path.realpath(helper) == os.path.realpath(auto_queue.__file__):

runpy.run_path(helper, run_name="__main__")
