    def successor(self, name="successor"):
        path = self.tmp / "attended" / name
        path.mkdir(parents=True)
        return path

    def test_transfer_from_blocked_is_final_and_offers_no_decision(self):
        """Revision 13 (item 10): `transfer JOB --to DIR --note TEXT` from Blocked makes the
        job Transferred: the report shows "transferred to DIR" and no decision; the decision
        and the note are kept in the record; the job cannot change afterwards (set, wait,
        criterion, candidate, worker start, transfer again); `set JOB Transferred` is not a
        way in; a missing successor directory is refused."""
        self.ok(self.set(ALPHA, "Preparing"))
        self.ok(self.set(ALPHA, "Blocked", "--note", "two fixes possible",
                         "--decision", "choose option a or b"))
        self.assertEqual(self.tool("set", BETA, "Transferred").returncode, 2)
        target = self.successor()
        result = self.tool("transfer", ALPHA, "--to", self.tmp / "no-such-dir", "--note", "x")
        self.refused(result, 2)
        self.assertEqual(self.state(ALPHA), "Blocked")
        result = self.ok(self.tool("transfer", ALPHA, "--to", target, "--note",
                                   "continued attended in the successor record"))
        self.assertIn(f"{ALPHA} Transferred to {target}", result.stdout)
        entry = job_entry(self.status(), ALPHA)
        self.assertEqual(entry["state"], "Transferred")
        self.assertEqual(entry["transfer"]["to"], str(target))
        self.assertEqual(entry["transfer"]["from_state"], "Blocked")
        self.assertEqual(entry["transfer"]["decision_needed_at_transfer"], "choose option a or b")
        self.assertNotIn("decision_needed", entry)
        report = self.report()
        self.assertEqual(self.result_cell(report, ALPHA), f"transferred to {target}")
        step = self.result_cell(report, ALPHA, column=2)
        self.assertNotIn("decision needed", step)
        self.assertNotIn("choose option", report)
        self.assertIn("Transferred to", (self.queue / "EVENTS.log").read_text())
        for args, code in ((("set", ALPHA, "Preparing"), 8), (("set", ALPHA, "Discarded"), 8),
                           (("wait", ALPHA, "--until", "2026-10-13T06:00:00Z"), 8),
                           (("criterion", ALPHA, "--file", self.criterion), 8),
                           (("candidate", ALPHA, "--repo", self.repo, "--commit", "HEAD"), 8),
                           (("worker", "start", ALPHA, "--id", "w-after"), 8),
                           (("transfer", ALPHA, "--to", target, "--note", "again"), 8)):
            with self.subTest(args=args[:2]):
                self.refused(self.tool(*args), code)
                self.assertEqual(self.state(ALPHA), "Transferred")

        """Revision 13 (item 10): transfer from Preparing is refused (9) while a worker for
        the job is registered, and the job stays Preparing; after `worker end` it is accepted.

    def write_fixture(self, path, data, writer=None):
        """Revision 15: write fixture bytes with `writer` (default: Path.write_bytes) and
        return what is then on disk. A step that reports success but leaves no file, or other
        bytes, is a test failure naming the file (revision 14 review finding 1: never
        FileNotFoundError)."""
        if path.exists():
            path.unlink()
        (writer or (lambda target, payload: target.write_bytes(payload)))(path, data)
        if not path.is_file():
            self.fail("the archive fixture step reported success but wrote no archive at %s"
                      % path)
        written = path.read_bytes()
        if written != data:
            self.fail("the archive fixture step wrote other bytes than intended at %s" % path)
        return written

    @staticmethod
    def archive_entries(data):
        """Revision 14: the members of an `!<arch>` archive as (header, name, content), the
        name read from BSD `#1/N` or GNU `name/` and `/N` forms; None if it does not parse."""
        if not data.startswith(b"!<arch>\n"):
            return None
        entries, pos, names = [], 8, b""
        while pos < len(data):
            header = data[pos:pos + 60]
            if len(header) < 60 or header[58:60] != b"`\n" or not header[48:58].strip().isdigit():
                return None
            size = int(header[48:58])
            body = data[pos + 60:pos + 60 + size]
            if len(body) < size:
                return None
            raw = header[:16].rstrip(b" ")
            if raw.startswith(b"#1/") and raw[3:].isdigit():
                length = int(raw[3:])
                name, content = body[:length].rstrip(b"\0"), body[length:]
            elif raw == b"//":
                names, name, content = body, raw, body
            elif raw.startswith(b"/") and raw[1:].isdigit() and names:
                name = names[int(raw[1:]):].split(b"/\n")[0]
                content = body
            else:
                name = raw[:-1] if raw.endswith(b"/") and raw != b"/" else raw
                content = body
            entries.append((header, name.decode("latin-1"), content))
            pos += 60 + size + (size % 2)
        return entries

    def archive_members_ok(self, data, members):
        """The archive's own members (index and name-table members left aside) are exactly
        `members`, in order, with these contents. macOS ar pads a member's content with up to
        seven newlines (inside its size) to keep 8-byte alignment; such padding is allowed."""
        entries = self.archive_entries(data)
        if entries is None:
            return False
        own = [(name, content) for _, name, content in entries
               if not (name.startswith("__.SYMDEF") or name in ("/", "//", "/SYM64"))]
        if [name for name, _ in own] != list(members):
            return False
        for (_, content), intended in zip(own, members.values()):
            rest = content[len(intended):]
            if not content.startswith(intended) or len(rest) > 7 or rest.strip(b"\n"):
                return False
        return True

    def dates_only_differ(self, first, second):
        """The two archives differ, and only in member header date fields (bytes 16-28)."""
        a, b = self.archive_entries(first), self.archive_entries(second)
        if first == second or a is None or b is None or len(a) != len(b):
            return False
        return all(x[0][:16] + x[0][28:] == y[0][:16] + y[0][28:] and x[2] == y[2]
                   for x, y in zip(a, b))

    def timestamp_archives(self, path, members, changed, same_size, style="gnu"):
        """Revision 15: (how, original, redated, changed, same_size) archive bytes for the
        timestamp test, written by the test (ar_archive, in the `style` layout; no ar or
        ranlib): the members dated 1000000000 (index 1000000007), the same members dated
        1100000000 (index 1100000007), and `changed` and `same_size` (a member changed
        without changing its size) dated 1100000000. Each is written to `path` and read back
        (write_fixture) and checked byte by byte: it holds exactly the intended members and
        contents, its index member comes first, and the re-dated one differs from the
        original in member header dates only. Any other result is a test failure that says
        which archive is wrong."""
        archives = []
        for contents, when in ((members, AR_DATE), (members, AR_REDATE), (changed, AR_REDATE),
                               (same_size, AR_REDATE)):
            archives.append(self.write_fixture(path, ar_archive(contents, when, style,
                                                                index_when=when + 7)))
        original, redated, after, same = archives
        for label, data, contents in (("original", original, members),
                                      ("re-dated", redated, members),
                                      ("content-changed", after, changed),
                                      ("same-size changed", same, same_size)):
            entries = self.archive_entries(data)
            if not self.archive_members_ok(data, contents):
                self.fail("the %s %s archive does not hold exactly the intended members"
                          % (label, style))
            index = "__.SYMDEF SORTED" if style == "bsd" else "/"
            if entries[0][1] != index:
                self.fail("the %s %s archive does not start with its index %r"
                          % (label, style, index))
        if not self.dates_only_differ(original, redated):
            self.fail("the re-dated %s archive differs from the original in more than the "
                      "member dates, or not at all" % style)
        return ("archives written by the test (%s layout)" % style, original, redated, after,
                same)

    def normalized_fingerprint_script(self, archive):
        """A fingerprint script printing the archive's exact digest and its normalized
        digest from payload/tools/fingerprint_normalize.py."""
        self.counter += 1
        path = self.work / f"fingerprint-ar-{self.counter}.py"
        normalizer = TOOL.parent / "payload" / "tools" / "fingerprint_normalize.py"
        path.write_text(f"""#!{sys.executable}
import hashlib, subprocess, sys
data = open({str(archive)!r}, "rb").read()
print("FINGERPRINT " + hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest())
out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", "-B", {str(normalizer)!r}, "file", "--kind",
                      "archive", {str(archive)!r}], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
print("NORMALIZED " + out.stdout.split()[0])
""")
        path.chmod(0o755)
        return path

    def exact(self, script):
        out = subprocess.run([str(script)], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
        return dict(line.split() for line in out.splitlines())

    def normalize(self, path, kind="archive"):
        """Revision 15: (digest, stderr) of payload/tools/fingerprint_normalize.py for one file."""
        normalizer = TOOL.parent / "payload" / "tools" / "fingerprint_normalize.py"
        out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", "-B", str(normalizer), "file", "--kind", kind,
                              str(path)], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
        return out.stdout.split()[0], out.stderr

    def test_install_check_classifies_timestamp_only_archive_change(self):
        """Revision 13 (item 13): for an archive, an exact match is available
        and records the normalized value; the same members re-archived with other dates
        change the exact fingerprint, and install check then says "timestamp-only
        differences: attended validation needed" but keeps the installation unavailable
        (12; runs refused; the recorded value is not replaced); a member whose content
        changed is not classified; restoring the exact bytes makes it available again.
        Revision 14 (review): also not a member whose content changed but not its size.
        Revision 15: the archives are written by the test (timestamp_archives) in both real
        layouts, GNU/SysV (with a `/` symbol table, a `//` long-name table and odd-size
        padding) and BSD/macOS (with a dated `__.SYMDEF SORTED` index, `#1/N` names and
        alignment padding), each on its own queue, on every platform; ar and ranlib are not
        used."""
        members = {"one.txt": b"first member\n", "two.txt": b"second member\n",
                   "a_member_with_a_long_name.o": b"long-named member\n"}
        changed_members = dict(members, **{"two.txt": b"second member, changed\n"})
        same_size_members = dict(members, **{"two.txt": b"SECOND member\n"})
        self.assertEqual(len(same_size_members["two.txt"]), len(members["two.txt"]))
        for style in ("gnu", "bsd"):
            with self.subTest(layout=style):
                if style != "gnu":
                    self.use_new_queue("q-archive-" + style)
                self.check_timestamp_only_archive(style, members, changed_members,
                                                  same_size_members)

    def check_timestamp_only_archive(self, style, members, changed_members, same_size_members):
        """The body of the test above for one archive layout, on the current queue."""
        self.prepare(BETA)
        archive = self.work / f"libsynthetic-{style}.a"
        how, original, redated, changed, same_size = self.timestamp_archives(
            archive, members, changed_members, same_size_members, style)
        archive.write_bytes(original)
        script = self.normalized_fingerprint_script(archive)
        values = self.exact(script)
        expect = values["FINGERPRINT"]
        self.ok(self.tool("install", "check", "--script", script, "--expect", expect))
        shown = json.loads(self.ok(self.tool("install", "show")).stdout)
        self.assertEqual(shown["state"], "available")
        self.assertEqual(shown["expected_normalized"], values["NORMALIZED"])
        archive.write_bytes(redated)
        self.assertNotEqual(self.exact(script)["FINGERPRINT"], expect, how)
        self.assertEqual(self.exact(script)["NORMALIZED"], values["NORMALIZED"], how)
        result = self.tool("install", "check", "--script", script, "--expect", expect)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 12, result.stdout + result.stderr)
        shown = json.loads(self.ok(self.tool("install", "show")).stdout)
        self.assertEqual(shown["state"], "unavailable")
        self.assertTrue(shown["reason"].startswith(
            "timestamp-only differences: attended validation needed"), shown["reason"])
        self.assertEqual(shown["expected"], expect)
        self.attempt(BETA, 12)
        self.assertIn("timestamp-only differences", self.report())
        archive.write_bytes(same_size)
        self.assertNotEqual(self.exact(script)["NORMALIZED"], values["NORMALIZED"], how)
        archive.write_bytes(changed)
        self.assertNotEqual(self.exact(script)["NORMALIZED"], values["NORMALIZED"], how)
        result = self.tool("install", "check", "--script", script, "--expect", expect)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 12, result.stdout + result.stderr)
        shown = json.loads(self.ok(self.tool("install", "show")).stdout)
        self.assertEqual(shown["reason"], "it no longer matches its recorded starting state")
        archive.write_bytes(original)
        self.ok(self.tool("install", "check", "--script", script, "--expect", expect))
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(self.ok(self.tool("install", "show")).stdout)["state"],
                         "available")
        self.attempt(BETA, 0)

    def test_normalizer_archive_fields_and_corruption(self):
        """Revision 15: the normalizer on archives written by the test, in both layouts. Only
        member header dates are ignored: the same members re-dated (the index too) give the
        same value; a changed member name, owner, index entry or member content (also of the
        same size), and a reordered member list, give another. Damaged archives (cut inside
        the last member, a short member header, bad header magic, a member size past the end,
        a size that is not a number, bad archive magic) are compared byte for byte, with
        "not a parsable archive" on stderr, so a damaged archive re-dated is never
        timestamp-only. Control: each undamaged pair has the same value."""
        members = {"one.txt": b"first member\n", "two.txt": b"second member\n",
                   "a_member_with_a_long_name.o": b"long-named member\n"}
        path = self.work / "fields.a"
        for style in ("gnu", "bsd"):
            with self.subTest(layout=style):
                base = ar_archive(members, AR_DATE, style, index_when=AR_DATE + 7)
                redated = ar_archive(members, AR_REDATE, style, index_when=AR_REDATE + 9)
                self.assertTrue(self.archive_members_ok(base, members))
                self.assertTrue(self.dates_only_differ(base, redated))
                self.write_fixture(path, base)
                reference, note = self.normalize(path)
                self.assertNotIn("not a parsable archive", note)
                self.assertNotEqual(reference, sha256_file(path))
                self.write_fixture(path, redated)
                self.assertEqual(self.normalize(path)[0], reference, "re-dated")
                reordered = dict(reversed(list(members.items())))
                variants = {
                    "member name": base.replace(b"two.txt", b"twX.txt", 1),
                    "owner": ar_archive(members, AR_DATE, style, index_when=AR_DATE + 7, uid=501),
                    "member order": ar_archive(reordered, AR_DATE, style, index_when=AR_DATE + 7),
                    "same-size content": ar_archive(dict(members, **{"two.txt": b"SECOND member\n"}),
                                                    AR_DATE, style, index_when=AR_DATE + 7),
                    "index entry": base.replace(b"sym_one", b"sym_ONE", 1)}
                for label in ("member name", "index entry"):  # the same bytes but one
                    self.assertEqual(len(variants[label]), len(base), label)
                for label, data in variants.items():
                    self.assertNotEqual(data, base, label)
                    self.write_fixture(path, data)
                    digest, note = self.normalize(path)
                    self.assertNotIn("not a parsable archive", note, label)
                    self.assertNotEqual(digest, reference, label)
                damaged_redated = ar_corruptions(redated)
                for label, data in ar_corruptions(base).items():
                    self.write_fixture(path, data)
                    digest, note = self.normalize(path)
                    self.assertIn("not a parsable archive; compared byte for byte", note, label)
                    self.assertEqual(digest, hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(), label)
                    self.write_fixture(path, damaged_redated[label])
                    self.assertNotEqual(self.normalize(path)[0], digest,
                                        "a damaged archive re-dated counted as timestamp-only: "
                                        + label)

    def test_archive_step_without_output_never_ends_in_file_not_found(self):
        """Revision 15 (revision 14 review, finding 1, the outside reader): a tool or step
        that reports success without writing the archive must lead to the stated fallback or
        a clear failure, never FileNotFoundError. (a) The reader's case: ar and ranlib
        stand-ins first on PATH that exit 0 and write nothing. With 1664dd1f's test code
        this ended in FileNotFoundError; now the archives are the intended ones (no outside
        tool is used). (b) The fixture's own write step replaced by one that returns without
        writing: a test failure that names the missing archive."""
        fakebin = self.work / "fake-ar-bin"
        fakebin.mkdir()
        for name in ("ar", "ranlib"):
            (fakebin / name).write_text("#!%s\nimport sys\nsys.exit(0)\n" % sys.executable)
            (fakebin / name).chmod(0o755)
        self.env["PATH"] = str(fakebin) + os.pathsep + self.env.get("PATH", os.defpath)
        members = {"one.txt": b"first member\n", "two.txt": b"second member\n"}
        changed = dict(members, **{"two.txt": b"second member, changed\n"})
        same_size = dict(members, **{"two.txt": b"SECOND member\n"})
        try:
            how, original, redated, after, same = self.timestamp_archives(
                self.work / "lib-no-output.a", members, changed, same_size)
        except FileNotFoundError as error:
            self.fail("an archive step that wrote nothing ended in FileNotFoundError: %s" % error)
        self.assertTrue(self.archive_members_ok(original, members), how)
        self.assertTrue(self.archive_members_ok(after, changed), how)
        self.assertTrue(self.archive_members_ok(same, same_size), how)
        self.assertTrue(self.dates_only_differ(original, redated), how)
        target = self.work / "never-written.a"
        with self.assertRaises(self.failureException) as caught:
            self.write_fixture(target, original, writer=lambda path, data: None)
        self.assertIn("wrote no archive at %s" % target, str(caught.exception))

    def test_install_check_expect_normalized_and_known_exit_codes(self):
        """Revision 13 (items 13, 14): on a queue with no stored normalized value,
        --expect-normalized gives the value to compare; the classification still leaves the
        installation unavailable. Exit 3 and exit 4 of a fingerprint script are named."""
        script = self.fingerprint_script("abc123")
        script.write_text(script.read_text().replace(
            'print("FINGERPRINT abc123")', 'print("FINGERPRINT abc123")\nprint("NORMALIZED n1")'))
        result = self.tool("install", "check", "--script", script, "--expect", "zzz999",
                           "--expect-normalized", "n1")
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 12, result.stdout + result.stderr)
        shown = json.loads(self.ok(self.tool("install", "show")).stdout)
        self.assertEqual(shown["state"], "unavailable")
        self.assertIn("timestamp-only differences", shown["reason"])
        result = self.tool("install", "check", "--script", script, "--expect", "zzz999",
                           "--expect-normalized", "n2")
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 12)
        self.assertNotIn("timestamp-only", self.ok(self.tool("install", "show")).stdout)
        for code, words in ((3, "a process runs from the installation"),
                            (4, "the process table could not be read")):
            with self.subTest(code=code):
                bad = self.fingerprint_script("zzz999", code)
                self.assertEqual(self.tool("install", "check", "--script", bad, "--expect",
                                           "zzz999").returncode, 12)
                reason = json.loads(self.ok(self.tool("install", "show")).stdout)["reason"]
                self.assertEqual(reason, f"its fingerprint script failed (exit {code}: {words})")

    def test_normalizer_build_time_masks_date_and_derived_fields(self):
        """Revision 13 (item 13): a bundle built twice from source differing only in an
        embedded asctime build date has a different exact digest and the same build-time
        digest (date, LC_UUID and code signature masked); a different other string changes
        it. A non-archive given as an archive is compared byte for byte.
        Revision 15: the bundles are written by the test (macho_bundle; formerly built with
        cc on macOS only), so this runs on every platform. Controls: the UUID and the
        signature range really differ between the two dates (so the masking is needed); a
        changed code byte, or one changed byte in the load commands (also LC_DYSYMTAB,
        LC_BUILD_VERSION and LC_LOAD_DYLIB, review finding 2), __cstring, __unwind_info, __DATA,
        or __LINKEDIT before the signature (also the fixups, exports trie, function starts,
        symbol and string tables), changes the digest; a changed byte inside the UUID or the
        signature range does not. The fixture's load commands are those of cc output, in
        order (MACHO_CC_COMMANDS)."""
        a = self.work / "a.so"
        a.write_bytes(macho_bundle())
        b = self.work / "b.so"
        b.write_bytes(macho_bundle(date="Tue Oct 13 01:02:03 2026"))
        c = self.work / "c.so"
        c.write_bytes(macho_bundle(extra="phasex"))
        seven = self.work / "seven.so"
        seven.write_bytes(macho_bundle(value=7))
        ranges = macho_ranges(a.read_bytes())
        for name in ("uuid", "signature"):
            begin, end = ranges[name]
            self.assertNotEqual(a.read_bytes()[begin:end], b.read_bytes()[begin:end], name)
        self.assertNotEqual(sha256_file(a), sha256_file(b))
        digest = self.normalize(a, "build-time")[0]
        self.assertEqual(self.normalize(b, "build-time")[0], digest)
        self.assertNotEqual(self.normalize(c, "build-time")[0], digest)
        self.assertNotEqual(self.normalize(seven, "build-time")[0], digest, "a code change")
        self.assertEqual(self.normalize(a, "archive")[0], sha256_file(a))
        original = a.read_bytes()
        changed = self.work / "changed.so"
        date_at = original.index(MACHO_DATE.encode())
        self.assertEqual(macho_load_commands(original), MACHO_CC_COMMANDS)
        for name, masked in (("text", False), ("cstring", False), ("unwind_info", False),
                             ("data", False), ("linkedit", False), ("fixups", False),
                             ("exports trie", False), ("function starts", False),
                             ("symbol table", False), ("string table", False),
                             ("dysymtab command", False), ("build version command", False),
                             ("load dylib command", False), ("commands", False),
                             ("uuid", True), ("signature", True)):
            begin, end = ranges[name]
            at = date_at + len(MACHO_DATE) + 2 if name == "cstring" else (begin + end) // 2
            with self.subTest(byte=name):
                data = bytearray(original)
                data[at] ^= 0x01
                changed.write_bytes(bytes(data))
                if masked:
                    self.assertEqual(self.normalize(changed, "build-time")[0], digest)
                else:
                    self.assertNotEqual(self.normalize(changed, "build-time")[0], digest)

    # ---- Revision 15 (review finding 4): real-tool conformance, where the tools exist ----------

    def real_tool(self, *names):
        """The paths of `names` on the test's PATH, or None when one is missing."""
        tools = [shutil.which(name, path=self.env.get("PATH")) for name in names]
        return tools if all(tools) else None

    @staticmethod
    def ar_family(ar):
        """Revision 15 (second reading, finding 1): "apple" for Apple (cctools) ar, whose
        `--version` prints its usage, "gnu" for GNU binutils ar, None for any other ar."""
        try:
            out = subprocess.run([ar, "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
        except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
            return None
        text = out.stdout + out.stderr
        if "GNU ar" in text or "GNU Binutils" in text:
            return "gnu"
        if text.lstrip().startswith("usage:") and "ar -d" in text:
            return "apple"
        return None

    def test_real_tool_conformance_archive(self):
        """Revision 15 (review finding 4): where `ar` and `ranlib` are on PATH, an archive they
        write must have what the normalizer and the fixtures rely on: it parses as `!<arch>`
        (no "not a parsable archive"); its members hold exactly the intended contents; whether
        the fixture of the matching layout (BSD `#1/N` names: ar_archive "bsd"; otherwise
        "gnu") has the same member name fields, sizes and contents (the index member aside: its
        contents depend on the symbols) is reported on stderr (revision 15, second reading,
        finding 1: another valid `ar`, for example llvm-ar, pads names differently); for every
        `ar`, re-dating every member header
        of the real archive keeps the normalized value and changes the exact digest, and one
        changed content byte changes the normalized value. These are the only uses of real
        tools in the kit's tests; without the tools the test is skipped with that reason, and
        the fixture tests above still run. A tool that fails or writes no archive is reported
        as a skip with its reason, never as FileNotFoundError. Revision 15 follow-up (GitHub's
        macOS runner): tools whose archive does not hold exactly the intended members (an `ar`
        or `ranlib` that drops or reorders members that are not object files) are reported as
        a skip naming the members found, and a layout that differs from the fixture's is only
        noted on stderr, for every `ar`; the normalizer checks on the real archive stay strict."""
        tools = self.real_tool("ar", "ranlib")
        if not tools:
            self.skipTest("real-tool conformance check skipped: ar and ranlib are not both on "
                          "PATH (the archive fixture tests do not need them)")
        ar, ranlib = tools
        members = {"one.txt": b"first member\n", "two.txt": b"second member\n",
                   "a_member_with_a_long_name.o": b"long-named member\n"}
        build = self.work / "real-ar"
        build.mkdir()
        for name, data in members.items():
            (build / name).write_bytes(data)
            os.utime(build / name, (AR_DATE, AR_DATE))
        archive = build / "libreal.a"
        for argv in ([ar, "rc", str(archive), *members], [ranlib, str(archive)]):
            done = subprocess.run(argv, cwd=build, capture_output=True, env=self.env)
            if done.returncode != 0 or not archive.is_file():
                self.skipTest("real-tool conformance check skipped: %s exited %d%s" % (
                    argv[0], done.returncode, "" if archive.is_file() else " and wrote no archive"))
        real = archive.read_bytes()
        print("\n[conformance] real archive from %s and %s (%d bytes)" % (ar, ranlib, len(real)),
              file=sys.stderr)
        entries = self.archive_entries(real)
        self.assertIsNotNone(entries, "the real archive does not parse as !<arch>")
        if not self.archive_members_ok(real, members):
            self.skipTest("real-tool conformance check skipped: %s and %s wrote an archive "
                          "without exactly the intended members (found %s)" % (
                              ar, ranlib, [(e[1], len(e[2])) for e in entries]))
        digest, note = self.normalize(archive)
        self.assertNotIn("not a parsable archive", note)
        style = "bsd" if any(e[0][:3] == b"#1/" for e in entries) else "gnu"
        fixture = self.archive_entries(ar_archive(members, AR_DATE, style))

        def own(items):
            return [(e[0][:16], e[0][48:58], e[2]) for e in items
                    if not (e[1].startswith("__.SYMDEF") or e[1] in ("/", "/SYM64"))]
        print("[conformance] %s ar (%s): %s with the %s fixture" % (
            self.ar_family(ar) or "other", ar, "same member layout" if own(fixture) == own(entries)
            else "member layout DIFFERS", style), file=sys.stderr)
        redated, pos = bytearray(real), 8
        while pos < len(redated):
            size = int(redated[pos + 48:pos + 58])
            redated[pos + 16:pos + 28] = b"%-12d" % (AR_REDATE + pos)
            pos += 60 + size + size % 2
        self.write_fixture(archive, bytes(redated))
        self.assertNotEqual(sha256_file(archive), hashlib.sha256(real).hexdigest())
        self.assertEqual(self.normalize(archive)[0], digest, "re-dated real archive")
        changed = bytearray(real)
        changed[real.index(b"second member")] ^= 0x01
        self.write_fixture(archive, bytes(changed))
        self.assertNotEqual(self.normalize(archive)[0], digest, "changed content byte")

    def test_real_tool_conformance_macho_bundle(self):
        """Revision 15 (review finding 4): on macOS where `cc` is on PATH, bundles it builds
        (`cc -bundle`) must have what the normalizer and the fixture rely on: an LC_UUID and
        one LC_CODE_SIGNATURE whose range ends at the end of __LINKEDIT and of the file, after
        the load commands; two builds differing only in the asctime date differ exactly and
        have the same build-time digest, with nothing reported unmasked; a code change
        (`return 7`) changes it. A load command sequence other than the fixture's
        (MACHO_CC_COMMANDS) is reported on stderr, so the fixture can be brought up to date; it
        does not fail the test. Skipped, with the reason, off macOS, without cc, or when cc
        cannot build a bundle."""
        cc = self.real_tool("cc")
        if sys.platform != "darwin" or not cc:
            self.skipTest("real-tool conformance check skipped: needs macOS and cc on PATH "
                          "(the Mach-O fixture tests do not need them)")

        def bundle(name, date, value=1):
            source = self.work / f"{name}.c"
            source.write_text(f'const char *build_time = "{date}";\nconst char *what = "phaser";\n'
                              f"int version(void) {{ return {value}; }}\n")
            out = self.work / f"{name}.so"
            done = subprocess.run([cc[0], "-bundle", "-o", str(out), str(source)],
                                  capture_output=True, text=True, env=self.env)
            if done.returncode != 0 or not out.is_file():
                self.skipTest("real-tool conformance check skipped: cc -bundle exited %d: %s"
                              % (done.returncode, done.stderr.strip()[:200]))
            return out
        a = bundle("ra", MACHO_DATE)
        b = bundle("rb", "Tue Oct 13 01:02:03 2026")
        seven = bundle("r7", MACHO_DATE, 7)
        data = a.read_bytes()
        types = macho_load_commands(data)
        print("\n[conformance] cc bundle load commands: %s" % " ".join(hex(t) for t in types),
              file=sys.stderr)
        if types != MACHO_CC_COMMANDS:
            print("[conformance] NOTE: differs from the fixture's MACHO_CC_COMMANDS %s"
                  % " ".join(hex(t) for t in MACHO_CC_COMMANDS), file=sys.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(types.count(0x1b), 1, "LC_UUID")
        self.assertEqual(types.count(0x1d), 1, "LC_CODE_SIGNATURE")
        ranges = macho_ranges(data)
        sizeofcmds = struct.unpack_from("<I", data, 20)[0]
        begin, end = ranges["signature"]
        self.assertEqual(end, len(data), "the signature does not end at the end of the file")
        self.assertGreaterEqual(begin, 32 + sizeofcmds)
        self.assertGreaterEqual(begin, ranges["linkedit"][0])
        self.assertNotEqual(sha256_file(a), sha256_file(b))
        (first, note), (second, other) = self.normalize(a, "build-time"), self.normalize(b, "build-time")
        self.assertNotIn("not masked", note + other)
        self.assertNotIn("no build-time date found", note + other)
        self.assertEqual(first, second, "two cc builds differing only in the date")
        self.assertNotEqual(self.normalize(seven, "build-time")[0], first, "a code change")

    def test_normalizer_masks_code_signature_only_at_the_end(self):
        """Checkpoint 3 (REVIEW_CP2 finding 4): two bundles that differ in code, whose
        LC_CODE_SIGNATURE load command is rewritten to declare the whole file
        (dataoff 0, datasize = file length), keep different build-time digests (the
        declared range is not masked, and stderr says so). Control: unmodified, the same
        two bundles also differ, and a signature at the end is still masked (see the
        test above). Checkpoint 5 (review CP3 finding 6): the same holds for a range
        from the end of the load commands to the end of the file, and for that range
        with __LINKEDIT also rewritten to cover it (it would overlap __TEXT); such a
        file is compared byte for byte. Revision 15: the bundles are written by the test
        (macho_bundle, code `mov w0, #1` and `mov w0, #7`; formerly built with cc on macOS
        only), so this runs on every platform."""

        def bundle(name, value):
            out = self.work / f"{name}.so"
            out.write_bytes(macho_bundle(value=value))
            return out

        def widen(path, how):
            data = bytearray(path.read_bytes())
            ncmds, sizeofcmds = struct.unpack_from("<II", data, 16)
            begin = 0 if how == "whole" else 32 + sizeofcmds
            offset, found = 32, False
            for _ in range(ncmds):
                cmd, size = struct.unpack_from("<II", data, offset)
                if cmd == 0x1d:  # LC_CODE_SIGNATURE
                    struct.pack_into("<II", data, offset + 8, begin, len(data) - begin)
                    found = True
                elif (cmd == 0x19 and how == "linkedit"
                      and data[offset + 8:offset + 24].rstrip(b"\0") == b"__LINKEDIT"):
                    struct.pack_into("<QQ", data, offset + 40, begin, len(data) - begin)
                offset += size
            self.assertTrue(found, "the bundle has no LC_CODE_SIGNATURE")
            path.write_bytes(bytes(data))

        def digest(path):
            return self.normalize(path, "build-time")
        for how in ("whole", "after-load-commands", "linkedit"):
            with self.subTest(range=how):
                one, seven = bundle(f"b1-{how}", 1), bundle(f"b7-{how}", 7)
                self.assertNotEqual(digest(one)[0], digest(seven)[0])  # control
                widen(one, how)
                widen(seven, how)
                self.assertNotEqual(sha256_file(one), sha256_file(seven))
                (first, note), (second, _) = digest(one), digest(seven)
                self.assertNotEqual(first, second, "a widened signature range hid a code change")
                self.assertIn("LC_CODE_SIGNATURE not masked", note)
                self.assertEqual(first, sha256_file(one))  # compared byte for byte


ISO = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"
# Revision 16: a python that stays (at most 60 s) and, with argv words NAME VALUE, first sets
# that environment variable for itself and re-executes (so its command line never holds
# NAME=VALUE); with "child NAME VALUE FILE" it starts such a python as its child with the
# variable, writes the child's pid to FILE and stays (unmarked itself); with "join GROUP FILE"
# it starts a python child in process group GROUP, writes its pid and stays (repair 1).
HOLD = """import os, subprocess, sys, time
args = sys.argv[1:]
if args[:1] == ["child"]:
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env[args[1]] = args[2]
    child = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(60)"], env=env,
                             stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    with open(args[3] + ".tmp", "w") as handle:
        handle.write(str(child.pid))
    os.replace(args[3] + ".tmp", args[3])
elif args[:1] == ["join"]:
    group = int(args[1])
    child = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(60)"],
                             preexec_fn=lambda: os.setpgid(0, group), stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    with open(args[2] + ".tmp", "w") as handle:
        handle.write(str(child.pid))
    os.replace(args[2] + ".tmp", args[2])
elif args[:1] == ["orphan"]:
    child = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(60)"],
                             preexec_fn=lambda: os.setpgid(0, 0), stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    with open(args[1] + ".tmp", "w") as handle:
        handle.write(str(child.pid))
    os.replace(args[1] + ".tmp", args[1])
    os._exit(0)
time.sleep(60)
"""


class ProcessFixture(unittest.TestCase):
    """Revision 16: real processes for the helper's single-process views and survivors(),
    with no queue and no git."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.tmp = Path(os.path.realpath(self.temp.name))
        self.hold = self.tmp / "hold.py"
        self.hold.write_text(HOLD)
        self.procs, self.stray, self.counter = [], [], 0
        self.addCleanup(self.kill_all)

    def kill_all(self):
        for proc in self.procs:
            if proc.poll() is None:
                proc.kill()
            proc.wait(5)
        for pid in self.stray:
            try:
                os.kill(pid, signal.SIGKILL)
            except (ProcessLookupError, PermissionError):
                pass

    def start(self, *args, **popen):
        proc = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, str(self.hold), *args], stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                                stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, **popen)
        self.procs.append(proc)
        return proc

    def wait_for(self, condition, what, timeout=TIMEOUT):
        deadline = time.time() + timeout
        while time.time() < deadline:
            if condition():
                return
            time.sleep(0.05)
        self.fail("timed out waiting for " + what)

    def zombie(self):
        proc = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "pass"], start_new_session=True)
        self.procs.append(proc)
        self.wait_for(lambda: status_of(proc.pid) == "zombie", "a zombie")
        return proc.pid

    def probe(self, source, *args, env=None):
        self.counter += 1
        script = self.tmp / f"probe-{self.counter}.py"
        script.write_text(source)
        result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", "-B", str(script), str(TOOL.parent),
                                 *[str(a) for a in args]], cwd=self.tmp, text=True,
                                capture_output=True, timeout=60, env=env)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stdout + result.stderr)
        return result.stdout.strip()

    def snapshot(self, spec):
        return self.probe(SNAPSHOT_PROBE, json.dumps(spec))

    def views(self, spec, *pids):
        out = json.loads(self.probe(VIEWS_PROBE, json.dumps(spec), *pids))
        return {int(pid): view for pid, view in out.items()}

    def survivors(self, record):
        self.counter += 1
        path = self.tmp / f"record-{self.counter}.json"
        path.write_text(json.dumps(record))
        return json.loads(self.probe(SURVIVORS_PROBE, path))["survivors"]

    def later_second(self, bound):
        """Wait until a newly started process's start time (whole seconds) is after BOUND."""
        def later():
            proc = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(5)"])
            try:
                return start_of(proc.pid) > bound
            finally:
                proc.kill()
                proc.wait(5)
        self.wait_for(later, "a start time later than %d" % bound)


@needs_psutil
class PsutilFaultMatrix(ProcessFixture):
    """Revision 16: every refusal of the process layer with psutil made to fail inside the
    helper's own process (FAULT_SETUP), each error type on each field a decision needs."""

    REFUSED = "refused 17 cannot read the process table"

    def test_process_list_failure_refuses(self):
        """psutil.pids() raising any error, or listing nothing (so not this process), makes
        the table unreadable (17); control: no fault gives a table."""
        self.assertTrue(self.snapshot({}).startswith("table "))
        for name in ("AccessDenied", "ZombieProcess", "NoSuchProcess", "OSError", "empty"):
            with self.subTest(pids=name):
                out = self.snapshot({"pids": name})
                self.assertTrue(out.startswith(self.REFUSED), out)
                self.assertIn("whether queue processes are alive is unknown", out)

    def test_needed_field_failures(self):
        """For each needed field (status, parent, start time, group id): AccessDenied and
        ZombieProcess refuse (17) whether they hit another process or this one;
        NoSuchProcess refuses while the re-check still finds the process (17, "still
        exists"), and counts it as gone only when the re-check finds it gone: then the table
        is readable without it (for other processes; this process missing refuses). The group
        id on macOS: getpgid failing with ESRCH (as for a process that is exiting or a zombie)
        is answered from the kernel record, so the table stays complete, whatever the
        re-check says; the test checks that separately (test_macos_group_from_kernel_record)."""
        for field in ("status", "ppid", "create_time", "pgid"):
            for name in ("AccessDenied", "ZombieProcess"):
                if field == "pgid" and name == "ZombieProcess":
                    continue  # os.getpgid fails with an OSError, never a psutil error
                for who in ("others", "own"):
                    with self.subTest(field=field, error=name, who=who):
                        out = self.snapshot({"fields": {field: name}, "who": who})
                        self.assertTrue(out.startswith(self.REFUSED), out)
            if field == "pgid" and sys.platform == "darwin":
                continue  # test_macos_group_from_kernel_record
            for who in ("others", "own"):
                with self.subTest(field=field, error="NoSuchProcess", who=who, recheck="exists"):
                    out = self.snapshot({"fields": {field: "NoSuchProcess"}, "who": who,
                                         "exists": True})
                    self.assertTrue(out.startswith(self.REFUSED), out)
            with self.subTest(field=field, error="NoSuchProcess", who="others", recheck="gone"):
                out = self.snapshot({"fields": {field: "NoSuchProcess"}, "who": "others",
                                     "exists": False})
                self.assertEqual(out.split()[:2], ["table", "1"], out)
            with self.subTest(field=field, error="NoSuchProcess", who="own", recheck="gone"):
                out = self.snapshot({"fields": {field: "NoSuchProcess"}, "who": "own",
                                     "exists": False})
                self.assertTrue(out.startswith(self.REFUSED), out)
                self.assertIn("but not this one", out)

    @unittest.skipUnless(sys.platform == "darwin", MACOS_ONLY + "the kernel record of a "
                         "process whose group getpgid refuses")
    def test_macos_group_from_kernel_record(self):
        """macOS refuses getpgid (ESRCH) for a process that is exiting (still running, not yet a
        zombie) and for a zombie; ps read the group from the kernel record, and so does the
        helper. Repair 1 (finding 4): with getpgid failing so for the test's own processes
        only (a live process in its own group, one in the test's group, a zombie, and the
        reading process itself), whether the re-check would find them or not, the table holds
        each of them with the group getpgid gives. Unrelated processes are not faulted, so
        processes that start and end meanwhile cannot change the outcome."""
        own_group = self.start(preexec_fn=lambda: os.setpgid(0, 0))
        same_group = self.start()
        zombie = self.zombie()
        for proc in (own_group, same_group):
            self.wait_for(lambda proc=proc: start_of(proc.pid) > 0, "a live process")
        targets = [own_group.pid, same_group.pid, zombie]
        script = ("import json, os, sys\nsys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])\nimport auto_queue\n"
                  + FAULT_SETUP + "\nspec = json.loads(sys.argv[2])\n"
                  "spec['who'] = spec['who'] + [os.getpid()]\n"
                  "truth = {p: os.getpgid(p) for p in spec['who'] if p != spec['zombie']}\n"
                  "truth[spec['zombie']] = spec['zombie']\n"
                  "install_faults(spec)\n"
                  "procs = auto_queue.snapshot()\n"
                  "print(json.dumps({p: (procs[p][1] if p in procs else None) for p in truth}))\n")
        for exists in (True, False):
            with self.subTest(exists=exists):
                groups = json.loads(self.probe(script, json.dumps(
                    {"fields": {"pgid": "NoSuchProcess"}, "who": targets, "exists": exists,
                     "zombie": zombie})))
                expected = {own_group.pid: own_group.pid, same_group.pid: os.getpgid(0),
                            zombie: zombie}
                for pid, group in expected.items():
                    self.assertEqual(groups[str(pid)], group, "group of %d" % pid)
                self.assertEqual(len(groups), 4)
                self.assertTrue(all(g is not None for g in groups.values()), groups)

    @unittest.skipUnless(sys.platform == "darwin", MACOS_ONLY + "the kernel record layout check")
    def test_kernel_record_layout_check_needs_parent_and_group_apart(self):
        """Repair 1 (finding 9), repair 2: the kernel-record layout is trusted only when
        checked on a process whose parent and group differ. In a reading process whose own
        parent is its group leader (parent and group equal) the helper checks a child it
        starts in its own session (its own Python, repair 3); when that child cannot be
        started, or never ends (killed and reaped after about 5 s, nothing left), the check fails and
        neither a group nor a start time is read from the kernel record (fail closed); with the
        child it passes (control), as it does where its own parent and group differ."""
        code = ("import json, os, sys\nsys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])\nimport auto_queue\n"
                "own = (os.getppid() == os.getpgid(0))\n"
                "if sys.argv[2] == 'nochild':\n"
                "    def refuse(*args, **kwargs):\n        raise OSError('no child (test)')\n"
                "    auto_queue.subprocess.Popen = refuse\n"
                "children = []\n"
                "if sys.argv[2] == 'stuck':\n"
                "    real = auto_queue.subprocess.Popen\n"
                "    def stuck(args, **kwargs):\n"
                "        child = real([sys.executable, '-c', 'import time; time.sleep(60)'], **kwargs)\n"
                "        children.append(child.pid)\n        return child\n"
                "    auto_queue.subprocess.Popen = stuck\n"
                "import time\nbegin = time.time()\n"
                "ok = auto_queue.kinfo_layout_ok()\n"
                "took = time.time() - begin\n"
                "def left(pid):\n"
                "    try:\n        os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)\n        return True\n"
                "    except ChildProcessError:\n        return auto_queue.psutil.pid_exists(pid)\n"
                "if sys.argv[2] == 'stuck':\n"
                "    print(json.dumps([ok, took, [p for p in children if left(p)], len(children)]))\n"
                "    sys.exit(0)\n"
                "try:\n    start = auto_queue.kernel_start(os.getpid())\n"
                "except Exception:\n    start = None\n"
                "print(json.dumps([own, ok, auto_queue.kernel_pgid(os.getpid()), start]))\n")
        leader = ("import os, subprocess, sys\nos.setpgid(0, 0)\n"
                  "sys.exit(subprocess.call(sys.argv[1:]))\n")
        script = self.tmp / "layout.py"
        script.write_text(code)
        for mode, layout in (("nochild", False), ("child", True)):
            with self.subTest(mode=mode):
                out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", leader, sys.executable, "-I", "-B",
                                      str(script), str(TOOL.parent), mode], text=True,
                                     capture_output=True, timeout=60)
                self.assertEqual(out.returncode, 0, out.stderr)
                own, ok, group, start = json.loads(out.stdout)
                self.assertTrue(own, "the reading process's parent is its group leader")
                self.assertEqual(ok, layout, out.stdout)
                self.assertEqual(group is not None, layout, out.stdout)
                self.assertEqual(start is not None, layout, out.stdout)
        own, ok, group, start = json.loads(self.probe(code, "child"))
        self.assertEqual((ok, group), (True, os.getpgid(0)), (own, ok, group))
        self.assertIsNotNone(start)
        # Repair 3 (reading 3, finding 1): a layout child that never ends is killed and reaped
        # after about 5 s, the check fails (closed), and no process is left.
        out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", leader, sys.executable, "-I", "-B",
                              str(script), str(TOOL.parent), "stuck"], text=True,
                             capture_output=True, timeout=60)
        self.assertEqual(out.returncode, 0, out.stderr)
        ok, took, left, started = json.loads(out.stdout)
        self.assertEqual((ok, left, started), (False, [], 1), out.stdout)
        self.assertGreater(took, 4)
        self.assertLess(took, 15)

    @unittest.skipUnless(sys.platform == "darwin", MACOS_ONLY + "psutil's macOS clock-step "
                         "adjustment of create_time")
    def test_start_time_unmoved_by_a_clock_step(self):
        """Repair 2 (reading 2, finding 1): psutil on macOS shifts create_time() by whole
        seconds when the boot time it read at import differs from the current one (after a
        clock step), so two helper processes could see one process start a second apart. The
        helper reads the kernel's p_starttime instead: with psutil's import-time boot value
        shifted by -1, +1 or +5 s in the reading process, a live process recorded by another
        process stays the same process (same_process True, process_start and the table's start
        unchanged) and stays counted from the run's tracked list."""
        live = self.start(start_new_session=True)
        self.wait_for(lambda: start_of(live.pid) > 0, "the live process")
        start, text = start_of(live.pid), lstart_of(live.pid)
        record = {"run_id": "clock-step", "wrapper_pid": os.getpid(),
                  "started": time.strftime(ISO, time.gmtime(start - 5)),
                  "tracked": [{"pid": live.pid, "start": start}]}
        path = self.tmp / "clock-record.json"
        path.write_text(json.dumps(record))
        code = ("import json, sys\nsys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])\nimport auto_queue\n"
                "from psutil import _psosx\n"
                "_psosx.INIT_BOOT_TIME = _psosx.boot_time() + float(sys.argv[2])\n"
                "pid, text = int(sys.argv[3]), sys.argv[4]\n"
                "record = json.load(open(sys.argv[5]))\n"
                "print(json.dumps([auto_queue.same_process(pid, text), auto_queue.process_start(pid),"
                " auto_queue.snapshot()[pid][3], pid in auto_queue.survivors(record),"
                " auto_queue.psutil.Process(pid).create_time()]))\n")
        for shift in (-1, 1, 5):
            with self.subTest(shift=shift):
                same, shown, table, counted, psutil_time = json.loads(
                    self.probe(code, shift, live.pid, text, path))
                self.assertNotEqual(int(psutil_time), start, "control: psutil's value moved")
                self.assertEqual((same, shown, table, counted), (True, text, start, True))

    def test_own_environment_alone_unreadable_refuses(self):
        """Repair 1 (reading 1, finding 1): on macOS the helper's own environment must be
        readable whatever its command line shows: environ() alone failing (AccessDenied,
        ZombieProcess or any other error) for this process, or for every process, refuses
        (17); an environment that lacks this process's own run-id marker refuses too.
        Controls: the same faults on other processes only leave a table with this process's
        marker; a missing marker where none is set is no refusal. Off macOS markers are not
        read: no refusal."""
        env = dict(os.environ, GC_AUTO_RUN_ID="own-marker")
        def run(spec, environment=env):
            return self.probe(SNAPSHOT_PROBE, json.dumps(spec), env=environment)
        darwin = sys.platform == "darwin"
        for name in ("AccessDenied", "ZombieProcess", "RuntimeError"):
            for who in ("own", "all"):
                with self.subTest(error=name, who=who):
                    out = run({"fields": {"environ": name}, "who": who})
                    if darwin:
                        self.assertTrue(out.startswith(self.REFUSED), out)
                        self.assertIn("cannot read the environment of process", out)
                    else:
                        self.assertTrue(out.startswith("table "), out)
            with self.subTest(error=name, who="others"):
                out = run({"fields": {"environ": name}, "who": "others"})
                self.assertTrue(out.startswith("table "), out)
                self.assertEqual(out.split()[2], "1" if darwin else "0", out)
        with self.subTest(marker="dropped"):
            out = run({"fields": {"environ": "DropMarker"}, "who": "own"})
            if darwin:
                self.assertTrue(out.startswith(self.REFUSED), out)
                self.assertIn("does not show its run-id marker", out)
            else:
                self.assertTrue(out.startswith("table "), out)
        with self.subTest(marker="none set"):
            plain = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != "GC_AUTO_RUN_ID"}
            out = run({"fields": {"environ": "DropMarker"}, "who": "own"}, plain)
            self.assertTrue(out.startswith("table "), out)

    def test_unexpected_exceptions_fail_closed(self):
        """Repair 1 (reading 1, finding 2): an exception psutil does not normally raise
        (RuntimeError) while listing the processes, or on a needed field of any process (also
        inside psutil's oneshot(), the reviewer's case of a replaced method), makes
        the table unreadable (17), never a traceback; on an environment of another process it
        drops that process's markers; a failing re-check counts the process as existing. In the
        single-process views it makes that field unreadable: a zombie with an unreadable
        status is alive, a live process with an unreadable start time is `unreadable`, and
        (Linux) an unreadable thread count keeps a zombie alive."""
        out = self.snapshot({"pids": "RuntimeError"})
        self.assertTrue(out.startswith(self.REFUSED), out)
        for field in ("status", "ppid", "create_time", "pgid", "oneshot"):
            with self.subTest(field=field):
                out = self.snapshot({"fields": {field: "RuntimeError"}, "who": "others"})
                self.assertTrue(out.startswith(self.REFUSED), out)
        out = self.snapshot({"fields": {"environ": "RuntimeError", "cmdline": "RuntimeError"},
                             "who": "others"})
        self.assertTrue(out.startswith("table "), out)
        out = self.snapshot({"fields": {"status": "NoSuchProcess"}, "who": "others",
                             "exists": "RuntimeError"})
        self.assertTrue(out.startswith(self.REFUSED), out)
        self.assertIn("still exists", out)
        live = self.start(preexec_fn=lambda: os.setpgid(0, 0))
        self.wait_for(lambda: start_of(live.pid) > 0, "the live process")
        zombie = self.zombie()
        view = self.views({"fields": {"status": "RuntimeError"}, "who": zombie}, zombie)[zombie]
        self.assertEqual((view[0], view[2], view[3]), (True, False, True), view)
        view = self.views({"fields": {"create_time": "RuntimeError"}, "who": live.pid},
                          live.pid)[live.pid]
        self.assertEqual(view, [True, "unreadable", False, True])
        view = self.views({"fields": {"num_threads": "RuntimeError"}, "who": zombie},
                          zombie)[zombie]
        if sys.platform.startswith("linux"):
            self.assertEqual((view[0], view[2]), (True, False), view)
        else:
            self.assertEqual(view, [False, None, True, False])

    def test_vanished_once_but_existing_is_read_again(self):
        """NoSuchProcess (or, for the group, ESRCH, as macOS gives for a process that exited
        after its status was read) on the first read of every other process, while the
        re-check (the real psutil.pid_exists) still finds it: the process is read once more
        and the table is readable, with every process; the same fault on every read, with a
        re-check that finds the process, refuses (17) (on macOS not for the group, which the
        kernel record then gives)."""
        whole = self.snapshot({})
        for field in ("status", "ppid", "create_time", "pgid"):
            with self.subTest(field=field):
                out = self.snapshot({"fields": {field: "NoSuchProcess"}, "who": "others",
                                     "once": True})
                self.assertTrue(out.startswith("table "), out)
                self.assertGreater(int(out.split()[1]), int(whole.split()[1]) // 2, out)
                if field == "pgid" and sys.platform == "darwin":
                    continue  # answered from the kernel record: test_macos_group_from_kernel_record
                out = self.snapshot({"fields": {field: "NoSuchProcess"}, "who": "others",
                                     "exists": True})
                self.assertTrue(out.startswith(self.REFUSED), out)

    def test_table_stays_readable_while_processes_exit(self):
        """Real processes exiting (and becoming zombies) while the table is read: 150
        snapshots in the helper's process, with a child that keeps starting short-lived
        processes, are all readable (none refuses 17)."""
        churn = ("import subprocess, sys, time\nend = time.time() + 20\nkids = []\n"
                 "while time.time() < end:\n"
                 "    kids.append(subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, '-c', 'pass']))\n"
                 "    if len(kids) > 20:\n        kids.pop(0).wait()\n"
                 "    time.sleep(0.01)\n")
        spawner = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", churn], stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        self.procs.append(spawner)
        loop = ("import json, sys, time\nsys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])\nimport auto_queue\n"
                "refused = []\nfor n in range(150):\n    auto_queue._SNAPSHOT['procs'] = None\n"
                "    try:\n        auto_queue.snapshot()\n"
                "    except auto_queue.Refused as error:\n        refused.append(str(error))\n"
                "print(json.dumps(refused))\n")
        refused = json.loads(self.probe(loop))
        self.assertEqual(refused, [], "%d of 150 snapshots refused" % len(refused))

    def test_zombie_start_time_unreadable_is_kept_live_one_refuses(self):
        """A zombie whose start time cannot be read stays in the table (start None, flagged);
        the same fault on a live process refuses (17)."""
        zombie = self.zombie()
        live = self.start()
        out = self.snapshot({"fields": {"create_time": "ZombieProcess"}, "who": zombie})
        self.assertTrue(out.startswith("table "), out)
        out = self.snapshot({"fields": {"create_time": "AccessDenied"}, "who": live.pid})
        self.assertTrue(out.startswith(self.REFUSED), out)

    def test_single_process_views_fail_safe(self):
        """process_exists, process_start, zombie_gone and group_alive (pid as group id) of a
        live process L and a zombie Z. Control: L is alive with a start time, Z is gone.
        An unreadable status (AccessDenied or ZombieProcess) makes Z alive everywhere (its
        group too, since the table is then unreadable); an unreadable start time of L
        (AccessDenied, ZombieProcess, or NoSuchProcess while it still exists) is
        `unreadable`, never gone; on Linux an unreadable thread count makes Z alive, while
        on macOS (no thread count needed) it changes nothing."""
        live = self.start(preexec_fn=lambda: os.setpgid(0, 0))
        self.wait_for(lambda: start_of(live.pid) > 0, "the live process")
        zombie = self.zombie()
        views = self.views({}, live.pid, zombie)
        self.assertEqual(views[live.pid], [True, lstart_of(live.pid), False, True])
        self.assertEqual(views[zombie], [False, None, True, False])
        for name in ("AccessDenied", "ZombieProcess"):
            with self.subTest(status=name):
                view = self.views({"fields": {"status": name}, "who": zombie}, zombie)[zombie]
                self.assertEqual((view[0], view[2], view[3]), (True, False, True), view)
        for name in ("AccessDenied", "ZombieProcess", "NoSuchProcess"):
            with self.subTest(create_time=name):
                view = self.views({"fields": {"create_time": name}, "who": live.pid},
                                  live.pid)[live.pid]
                self.assertEqual(view[:3], [True, "unreadable", False], view)
                self.assertTrue(view[3])
        view = self.views({"fields": {"num_threads": "AccessDenied"}, "who": zombie},
                          zombie)[zombie]
        if sys.platform.startswith("linux"):
            self.assertEqual((view[0], view[2]), (True, False), view)
        else:
            self.assertEqual(view, [False, None, True, False])


@needs_psutil
class SurvivorsSingleRules(ProcessFixture):
    """Revision 16 (revision 15 reading, note 11): one test per attribution rule of
    survivors(), each with a process that only that rule attributes to the run: its parent is
    the wrapper (or process 1 or a subreaper standing in for the wrapper), so the descendant
    rule does not reach it, and no other rule matches it. Switching off that one rule fails
    the test (mutants in the job's CONTROLS.log)."""

    RUN = "single-rule-run"

    def record(self, earliest, **fields):
        record = {"run_id": self.RUN, "wrapper_pid": os.getpid(),
                  "started": time.strftime(ISO, time.gmtime(earliest - 5))}
        record.update(fields)
        return record

    def test_group_rule(self):
        """A member of the CMD's process group G (leader exited) that is the wrapper's child in
        another session than G: only the group rule (pgid in the leaders) counts it."""
        leader = self.start(preexec_fn=lambda: os.setpgid(0, 0))
        self.wait_for(lambda: start_of(leader.pid) > 0, "the leader")
        group, leader_start = leader.pid, lstart_of(leader.pid)
        member = self.start(preexec_fn=lambda: os.setpgid(0, group))
        self.wait_for(lambda: ppid_of(member.pid) == str(os.getpid()), "the member")
        leader.kill()
        leader.wait(5)
        self.assertEqual(os.getpgid(member.pid), group)
        self.assertNotEqual(os.getsid(member.pid), group)
        record = self.record(start_of(member.pid), pgid=group, process_start=leader_start)
        self.assertIn(member.pid, self.survivors(record))
        self.assertNotIn(member.pid, self.survivors(dict(record, pgid=group + 100000)))  # control

    def test_ancestry_gate(self):
        """Repair 1 (reading 1, finding 6): a member M of the CMD's process group G (leader
        exited) is counted by the group rule only when M is a leader or its parent is process
        1, the wrapper or a leader. Here M's parent P is an unrelated live process in the
        test's group, not counted itself: M is not counted. Control: with P as the run's
        wrapper (so M's parent is a root), M is counted."""
        leader = self.start(preexec_fn=lambda: os.setpgid(0, 0))
        self.wait_for(lambda: start_of(leader.pid) > 0, "the leader")
        group, leader_start = leader.pid, lstart_of(leader.pid)
        pidfile = self.tmp / "joined.pid"
        parent = self.start("join", str(group), str(pidfile))
        self.wait_for(pidfile.exists, "the joined member")
        member = int(pidfile.read_text())
        self.stray.append(member)
        leader.kill()
        leader.wait(5)
        self.assertEqual(os.getpgid(member), group)
        self.assertEqual(ppid_of(member), str(parent.pid))
        self.assertNotEqual(os.getpgid(parent.pid), group)
        record = self.record(start_of(parent.pid), pgid=group, process_start=leader_start)
        found = self.survivors(record)
        self.assertNotIn(member, found, "a group member whose parent is no root was counted")
        self.assertNotIn(parent.pid, found)
        self.assertIn(member, self.survivors(dict(record, wrapper_pid=parent.pid)))  # control

    def test_session_rule(self):
        """A process in the session S of the CMD (leader S exited) but in its own group, now
        an orphan: only the session rule (sid in the leaders) counts it."""
        pidfile = self.tmp / "orphan.pid"
        shell = self.start("orphan", str(pidfile), start_new_session=True)
        self.assertEqual(shell.wait(TIMEOUT), 0)
        session = shell.pid
        orphan = int(pidfile.read_text())
        self.stray.append(orphan)
        self.wait_for(lambda: ppid_of(orphan) not in ("", str(session)), "the orphan's new parent")
        self.assertEqual((os.getsid(orphan), os.getpgid(orphan)), (session, orphan))
        parent = int(ppid_of(orphan))
        record = self.record(start_of(orphan), pgid=session,
                             wrapper_pid=parent if parent != 1 else os.getpid())
        self.assertIn(orphan, self.survivors(record))
        self.assertNotIn(orphan, self.survivors(dict(record, pgid=session + 100000)))  # control

    @unittest.skipIf(sys.platform != "darwin", MACOS_ONLY + "run-id markers are read on macOS "
                     "only (Linux ps had no -E)")
    def test_marker_rule(self):
        """A process in its own session carrying the run's marker in its environment (not on
        its command line), the wrapper's child: only the marker rule counts it."""
        marked = self.start(env=dict(os.environ, GC_AUTO_RUN_ID=self.RUN), start_new_session=True)
        self.wait_for(lambda: start_of(marked.pid) > 0, "the marked process")
        record = self.record(start_of(marked.pid))
        self.assertIn(marked.pid, self.survivors(record))
        self.assertNotIn(marked.pid, self.survivors(dict(record, run_id="another-run")))  # control

    @unittest.skipIf(sys.platform != "darwin", MACOS_ONLY + "run-id markers are read on macOS "
                     "only (Linux ps had no -E)")
    def test_marked_parent_chain_rule(self):
        """An unmarked process P in its own session (the wrapper's child) whose child carries
        the marker: only the marked-parent chain counts P."""
        pidfile = self.tmp / "marked.pid"
        parent = self.start("child", "GC_AUTO_RUN_ID", self.RUN, str(pidfile),
                            start_new_session=True)
        self.wait_for(pidfile.exists, "the marked child")
        child = int(pidfile.read_text())
        self.stray.append(child)
        record = self.record(start_of(parent.pid))
        found = self.survivors(record)
        self.assertIn(child, found)
        self.assertIn(parent.pid, found)

    def test_tracked_list_rule(self):
        """A process in its own session, the wrapper's child, unmarked, in the run's tracked
        list with its start time: only the tracked rule counts it; with another start time it
        is not counted (reused pid)."""
        tracked = self.start(start_new_session=True)
        self.wait_for(lambda: start_of(tracked.pid) > 0, "the tracked process")
        start = start_of(tracked.pid)
        record = self.record(start, tracked=[{"pid": tracked.pid, "start": start}])
        self.assertIn(tracked.pid, self.survivors(record))
        record["tracked"][0]["start"] = start + 1
        self.assertNotIn(tracked.pid, self.survivors(record))  # control

    def test_probe_window_rule(self):
        """Members of the probe's group Q, each the wrapper's child: one started before the
        probe window's start (less the one-second allowance), one inside it, one after its
        end. Only the one inside is counted; switching off either bound of the window counts
        another."""
        probe = self.start(preexec_fn=lambda: os.setpgid(0, 0))
        self.wait_for(lambda: start_of(probe.pid) > 0, "the probe leader")
        group = probe.pid
        before = self.start(preexec_fn=lambda: os.setpgid(0, group))
        self.wait_for(lambda: ppid_of(before.pid) == str(os.getpid()), "the early member")
        self.later_second(start_of(before.pid) + 1)
        inside = self.start(preexec_fn=lambda: os.setpgid(0, group))
        self.wait_for(lambda: ppid_of(inside.pid) == str(os.getpid()), "the member inside")
        window = start_of(inside.pid)
        self.assertLess(start_of(before.pid), window - 1)
        self.later_second(window)
        after = self.start(preexec_fn=lambda: os.setpgid(0, group))
        self.wait_for(lambda: ppid_of(after.pid) == str(os.getpid()), "the late member")
        self.assertGreater(start_of(after.pid), window)
        for pid in (before.pid, inside.pid, after.pid):
            self.assertEqual(os.getpgid(pid), group)
        record = self.record(start_of(probe.pid), probe_pgid=group,
                             probe_start=lstart_of(probe.pid),
                             probe_started=time.strftime(ISO, time.gmtime(window)),
                             probe_ended=time.strftime(ISO, time.gmtime(window)))
        found = self.survivors(record)
        self.assertIn(inside.pid, found)
        self.assertNotIn(before.pid, found, "a member started before the probe window")
        self.assertNotIn(after.pid, found, "a member started after the probe window")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

tests/tst_publication_precheck_v20.py

"""Controls for the claims that publication_precheck.py makes (SPEC_A section 2).

The tool is only ever run through subprocess; nothing here imports it. Every
`check` call is bracketed by a snapshot of the work repository (HEAD, refs,
local config, working tree, FETCH_HEAD) and of the bare remote, which must be
identical before and after: the tool is read-only unless --fetch is named.
All Git state lives under a temporary directory, and the Developer's real Git
configuration is kept out with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM.
"""

import itertools
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

TOOL = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "payload" / "tools" / "publication_precheck.py"
HEX = "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567"
KEYS = ("repository", "remote", "remote_url", "base", "commit", "tree", "refspec")



def fake_git_script(real_git, calls, trigger, out, err, code):
    """Revision 15: the text of a Python test double for git (formerly /bin/sh). A call whose
    argument words include every word of `trigger` appends its words (space-joined) to the
    file `calls`, prints the lines `out` to stdout and `err` to stderr and exits `code`; every
    other call is replaced by the real git with the same arguments."""
    return ("#!%s\n" % sys.executable
            + "# test double: one intercepted git question; every other call is the real git\n"
            + "import os, sys\n"
            + "args = sys.argv[1:]\n"
            + "if all(word in args for word in %r):\n" % (tuple(trigger),)
            + "    with open(%r, 'a') as log:\n" % str(calls)
            + "        log.write(' '.join(args) + '\\n')\n"
            + "    for line in %r:\n" % (list(out),)
            + "        print(line)\n"
            + "    for line in %r:\n" % (list(err),)
            + "        print(line, file=sys.stderr)\n"
            + "    sys.exit(%d)\n" % code
            + "os.execv(%r, [%r] + args)\n" % (real_git, real_git))


def git_environment(home):
    """An environment in which git sees no personal or system configuration."""
    environment = {key: value for key, value in os.environ.items()
                   if not key.startswith("GIT_") and key != "XDG_CONFIG_HOME"}
    environment.update(GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=os.devnull, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM="1",
                       HOME=str(home), GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT="0", LC_ALL="C")
    return environment


# Revision 16: `check` and `outgoing` read a git repository; without git on PATH their tests
# skip with this reason (`vet` needs no git), and NoGitRefusal checks the tool's refusal.
GIT_SKIP = ("git not on PATH: the check and outgoing tests need git repositories; the tool "
            "refuses those commands without git (NoGitRefusal)")


@unittest.skipIf(shutil.which("git") is None, GIT_SKIP)
class PrecheckFixture(unittest.TestCase):
    """A work repository one commit ahead of a bare remote it tracks."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(self.temp.name).resolve()
        home = self.root / "home"
        home.mkdir()
        self.env = git_environment(home)
        self.bare = self.root / "remote.git"
        self.repo = self.root / "work"
        self.git("init", "-q", "--bare", str(self.bare), cwd=self.root)
        self.git("symbolic-ref", "HEAD", "refs/heads/master", cwd=self.bare)
        self.repo.mkdir()
        self.git("init", "-q", cwd=self.repo)
        self.git("symbolic-ref", "HEAD", "refs/heads/master", cwd=self.repo)
        self.configure_user(self.repo)
        self.git("remote", "add", "origin", str(self.bare), cwd=self.repo)
        self.base = self.commit_file(self.repo, "a.txt", "base\n", "base")
        self.git("push", "-q", "origin", "master", cwd=self.repo)
        self.git("fetch", "-q", "origin", cwd=self.repo)
        self.commit = self.commit_file(self.repo, "a.txt", "change\n", "change")
        self.tree = self.git("rev-parse", f"{self.commit}^{{tree}}", cwd=self.repo)
        self.assertEqual(self.git("rev-parse", "refs/remotes/origin/master", cwd=self.repo),
                         self.base)
        self.outgoing = self.root / "OUTGOING.txt"
        self.outgoing.write_text(self.block())

    def git(self, *words, cwd):
        result = subprocess.run(["git", *words], cwd=cwd, env=self.env,
                                text=True, capture_output=True)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        return result.stdout.strip()

    def configure_user(self, repo):
        self.git("config", "user.name", "Test Writer", cwd=repo)
        self.git("config", "user.email", "writer@example.invalid", cwd=repo)

    def commit_file(self, repo, name, content, message):
        (repo / name).write_text(content)
        self.git("add", name, cwd=repo)
        self.git("commit", "-q", "-m", message, cwd=repo)
        return self.git("rev-parse", "HEAD", cwd=repo)

    def block(self, **fields):
        """One OUTGOING.txt block (SPEC_A 1.2) bound to the fixture repository."""
        values = dict(repository="example_project", remote="origin", remote_url=str(self.bare),
                      base=self.base, commit=self.commit, tree=self.tree)
        values.update(fields)
        values.setdefault("refspec", f"{values['commit']}:refs/heads/master")
        return "".join(f"{key}: {values[key]}\n" for key in KEYS)

    def snapshot(self):
        work = [self.git(*words, cwd=self.repo) for words in (
            ("rev-parse", "HEAD"), ("for-each-ref",), ("config", "--list", "--local"),
            ("status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=all"))]
        fetch_head = self.repo / ".git" / "FETCH_HEAD"
        work.append((fetch_head.read_bytes(), fetch_head.stat().st_mtime_ns)
                    if fetch_head.exists() else None)
        remote = [self.git(*words, cwd=self.bare) for words in (
            ("for-each-ref",), ("config", "--list", "--local"))]
        return work, remote

    def check(self, *options, fetch=False):
        """Run `check` and prove it changed nothing (with --fetch: nothing but
        remote-tracking refs and FETCH_HEAD)."""
        before = self.snapshot()
        result = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-I", "-B", str(TOOL), "check", str(self.repo),
             str(self.outgoing), *options],
            env=self.env, cwd=self.root, text=True, capture_output=True)
        after = self.snapshot()
        if not fetch:
            self.assertEqual(after, before, "check changed Git state")
        else:
            self.assertEqual(after[1], before[1], "fetch changed the remote")
            for index in (0, 2, 3):
                self.assertEqual(after[0][index], before[0][index])
            self.assertEqual([line for line in after[0][1].splitlines() if "refs/remotes/" not in line],
                             [line for line in before[0][1].splitlines() if "refs/remotes/" not in line])
        return result

    def advance_remote(self):
